stories.primary_headline: ‘Classic case of diseased versus guilty mind’: Tihar jail psychiatrist on Lindsay Clancy row

primary_source.headline: ‘Classic case of diseased versus guilty mind’: Tihar jail psychiatrist on Lindsay Clancy row
primary_source.content:
A US court of justice is currently deciding the fate of a woman who had killed her three children in an alleged fit of postpartum psychosis, a severe mental illness that can take one away from reality.The jury is currently deliberating on the horrific killings that happened on the evening of January 24, 2023, in a Massachusetts house, with both the defendant and the prosecution having offered their closing statements last week.While the accused has not denied killing her children, she has pleaded ‘not guilty’ by reason of insanity.The case has divided the Americans, some say it was a calculated murder, others call it a terrible tale of neglected postpartum medical needs.It is one of the incidences where the boundary between a guilty and diseased mind gets blurred. To understand how a justice system navigates truth in such complex cases, DH spoke to Dr Vivek Rustagi, a senior psychiatrist at Tihar jail.The psychiatrist has also been associated with cases of national importance like ‘Delhi Rape Case’ (2012) and ‘Butcher of Delhi’.Lindsay Clancy’s case brings neglected 'postpartum psychosis' back into spotlight
The unique case of Lindsay ClancyLindsay Clancy, a 36-year-old woman from Massachusetts was charged with murder of her three children: Cora (5), Dawson (3) and Callan (8 months) in 2023 and since then the accused has been in custody.A trained labor and delivery nurse, Lindsay was living with her children and husband, Patrick Clancy, who is an IT professional and worked mostly from a fully ‘finished’ basement in the house.The family was apparently having a normal life until the middle of September 2022 when Lindsay started to see her mental health getting worse every passing day.Reportedly, she had no recorded history of mental illness, but her second childbirth had some reported physical complications.The accused reportedly went from one doctor to another, changed medicines frequently, had poor sleep and an unsettled anxiety.As per reports, she also briefly got herself into a psychiatric ward in January 2023, in the same time when she had disclosed to her kin that she had ‘scary thoughts’ or a suicidal ideation.&nbsp;However, there is no official documentation for the same other than anecdotal evidence from the family members.On January 24 (2023), she killed her children in the basement using exercise bands and later threw herself out of a second storey window that opened in her bedroom.The act was committed when her husband was shortly away from home to receive a food parcel ordered by Lindsay.&nbsp;While the children couldn’t be rescued in time, Lindsay has become paralyzed from down the waistline.Defendant versus prosecutionAs the case reached to courtroom trials, Lindsay’s lawyer Kevin Reddington maintained that the accused was so mentally ill that she should not be held criminally responsible for the act.To rest his case, he argued that the accused was overmedicated.The defendant also said that the accused had ‘command hallucinations’ or a ‘male voice’ instructing her to kill the kids first so she could kill herself next.However, the prosecution presented it as a case of planned homicide with a motive to get rid of the kids who apparently were a burden to her fragile mental health.Sick mind versus criminal responsibilityWhile mental health disorders may cause people to act in unacceptable ways, it is also common for some with a criminal intent to hide their ill motives behind an unstable mind. Experts have called it ‘malingering’ or fabrication of symptoms for non-medical benefits like escaping legal punishment.DH spoke to Dr Vivek Rustagi to understand postpartum mood disorders, how rationality can coexist in an ill mind, and what justice looks like in such cases.Reporter: What are postpartum mood disorders and how often do women get them?Psychiatrist: To start with, not all women will have postpartum mood disorders. It is not a clinical certainty.&nbsp;For others, the clash of a hormonal surge with changing brain chemistry during childbirth can cause abrupt mood changes.In most frequent cases (nearly 50 per cent), we see new mothers having ‘baby blues’ or a short period of mood fluctuation or low feelings. However, it may fade away on its own in a few weeks and the emotional stability gets restored.Then we have postpartum depression, a relatively severe form of mood disorder. It isn’t as common as baby blues. The woman can have a longer stretch of low mood which can extend up to some months, she can feel fatigued or mentally detached from the child. This often needs to be ruled out by an attending doctor.Postpartum psychosis is a very rare but much dangerous manifestation or complication. It can take her away from reality, she may feel agitated, experience a surge of energy, get restless, won’t sleep much, see or hear things which aren’t there (hallucinations) or start having false beliefs (delusions).&nbsp;At this point, it requires immediate medical intervention as the situation becomes a threat to both the mother and the newborn.Reporter: From the face of it, do you think Lindsay suffered from postpartum psychosis?Psychiatrist: I haven’t evaluated the accused in person, so it would be unfair to make a diagnosis.But, following the trials, I do have some reasons to believe it may not be postpartum psychosis.The very word ‘postpartum’ is the clue. The condition needs to manifest in early weeks of childbirth or it is safe to say at least in the first few months after childbirth. If the symptoms arise four months after nursing the newborn, the element of ‘postpartum’ becomes weak in the clinical context because the hormonal surge caused by pregnancy tends to subside by this time.However, I am not implying that the accused may not have been ill.Some trial representatives have called it generalized anxiety disorder, others have hinted about bipolar disorder. So, exact pinpointing is hard and unfair on my part.I would hesitate to call it a bipolar disorder as no manic episodes have been officially documented in the public record.From the face of it, using my industry knowledge, it looks more like a depression that gradually progressed into psychosis, maybe due to neglected care or maybe due to the alleged irregular intake of drugs.Reporter: Can psychosis occur with both depression and mania?Psychiatrist: Mental health disorders vastly vary in their presentation. Not all conditions take one away from reality but some do and brain chemistry plays a role in it.There are people with unipolar disorders like depression where the mood remains consistently low. Then we have bipolar disorder where there are fluctuating episodes of hyperactivity with low mood.Both depression and bipolar disorder can have psychotic symptoms if left untreated or aggravated.Also, the type of psychosis one experiences will be consistent with the mood disorder in the picture. It could look like hyperactivity, a chaotic state of mind or it could be more mood flattening in nature.For instance, in people with depression, psychosis bends towards the affected having more nihilistic or pessimistic delusions, assuming things like their body is rotting from inside or their kids are becoming very sick.&nbsp;Sometimes, psychosis can show up as grandiose thoughts like thinking one is a messenger of God or things like that. It may look more socially disorganized so to say.In my practice, postpartum psychosis looked more like severe agitation and restlessness in a woman than having an entirely dull expression.This is another reason I think Lindsay less likely had postpartum mood disorder.&nbsp;Reporter: Lindsay reportedly engaged with people normally, seemed unusually calm on the day of killings and took their lives in a logical sequence. Can rationality co-exist with mental illness?Psychiatrist: This is where things get extremely tricky. The entire case rests on this dilemma if the accused planned an efficient homicide or the act was a ritual fanned by her delusions.The defendant has argued that Lindsay had ‘command hallucinations’, although not clinically documented.As per my industry knowledge, command hallucinations are difficult to oppose by the affected. They appear as strong, authoritative voices in one’s mind that are hard to&nbsp; ignore.Many patients having psychosis may have delusions and hallucinations but other functional aspects of their mind may work just fine.It may not be surprising if the accused was able to hold normal conversations, do housekeeping chores in the background of the storm raging inside her head.The unusual calmness can also be true in some cases where the affected has finally submitted to their delusions and the mental conflict has eased down.&nbsp;In fact, this is why some people who commit suicide turn abnormally calm. They have made up their mind and there is no turning back.Reporter: How does a justice body approach such cases?Psychiatrist: Having been a part of such cases, a justice system may primarily look for 'mensrea' or a criminal intent.In Lindsay’s trial, her primary motive to kill her children will be accounted for.If the motive is overlapping with her delusions induced by the illness, such as her killing them thinking her kids would be unsafe on Earth without a mother nursing them or feeling they are more safe when dead, then her intent, though seemingly cruel, is coming from a psychologically twisted place to create greater good.Hence, she may get proven ‘non guilty’ under the provision of insanity.Reporter: How will the United States approach this case? Is there any standard way of testifying insanity in courtrooms?Psychiatrist: The United States does not have a uniform code of testifying insanity in criminal cases.It can vary from state to state and from case to case.In Massachusetts where the ongoing trials are being held, the courts may more commonly use a standard similar to the Model Penal Code which provides insanity defense under some circumstances. However, it cannot be said for certain what code is being used in this particular case.It states that a person is not responsible for criminal conduct if at the time of the act, a mental disease or defect caused them to lack the capacity to ‘appreciate’ the wrongfulness of their conduct or conform their actions to the law of the land.There are many other codes that can testify insanity in the US courts such as the McNaughton rule (a bit more rigid in expression), irresistible impulse, Durham rule (not guilty by reason of insanity) and others.Sometimes, they may apply different codes to come up with a verdict.Reporter: How does the Indian judicial system testify insanity?Psychiatrist: India strictly abides by the McNaughton rules which exempts a person on grounds of insanity if the person did not ‘know’ if their actions were legally wrong. It could be due to a defect of reason or a diseased mind.The provision is codified in Section 84 of the Indian Penal Code (IPS) and carried forward as Section 22 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.Reporter: How does testifying insanity differ between India and the United States?Psychiatrist: The US judiciary bodies take a relatively different approach to assess criminal intent.Unlike McNaughton rules which rely on the extreme polarity of actions (the person must know if their action was either right or wrong)(know or don’t know about its wrongfulness), the Model Penal Code (MPC) makes space for a social and emotional knowing whether an act was right or wrong.Unlike India, the US does not oversimplify intent but accepts it as a layered concept which is governed by many social and emotional factors.&nbsp;In fact, the Model Penal Code (MPC) is a moderate adaptation of McNaughton rules and volitional or irresistible impulse which exempts a person of criminal responsibility if defect of reason or mind has left them in no power to control their impulses or compulsive urges to conform to their conduct to the law.Hence, if you look closely, the US has carefully replaced the word ‘know’ with ‘appreciate’.The Indian judicial system relies more on the absolute knowing or not knowing the wrongfulness of their actions in relation to the law.Reporter: What factors make the case more favorable for Lindsay?Psychiatrist: There are many factors that can go in favor of Lindsay Clancy.To start with, in Massachusetts, the state where the case is being presented, the burden of proving a criminal intent rests on the prosecution and not the defendant.&nbsp;A defendant is presumed to be innocent and is not required to prove their lack of criminal intent or insanity.&nbsp;The entire burden falls on the prosecution which has to convince the jury that there is no other reasonable justification of the act other than the criminal intent of the defendant.In Lindsay’s trial, there is a previous documentation of symptoms and prescriptions, no strong motive to kill children and no prior history of drug abuse.Also, her trying to jump off the window and kill herself can be taken as ‘extended suicide’.All these factors make the legal proceedings more favorable towards her.However, since the verdict is awaited, it would be too soon to jump on any conclusion.Reporter: What can work against her?Psychiatrist: The prosecution has argued that her orchestrating the killings in an allegedly ‘planned’ manner and in absence of the husband shows an active conscience and brings an element of ‘concealment’ to the case.There is a term for it, we call it ‘Deliberate premeditation’ which means the action was planned and not performed in an impulse or an uncontrollable urge.Reporter: As per reports, the accused was asked to discontinue Zoloft 50 mg by her attending psychiatrist Dr Jennifer Tufts when she had reported side effects. Do all psychiatric drugs need to be tapered down? Do you agree that the alleged ‘drug cocktail’ caused her psychosis?Psychiatrist: There are many psychiatric drugs, including the SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor) which are not abruptly stopped but have to be tapered down just like a diabetes medicine or a blood pressure pill.But there are some which can be discontinued, particularly if they are low dosage.Zoloft 50 mg is a relatively low dose prescription and it is common and rather safe for psychiatrists to ask people to discontinue if they are reporting any side effects.All medicines come with side effects which are extremely rare and hardly apply to most of the population.Interestingly, antimalarial medicine can make a person go into psychosis in rarest of cases.Also, psychiatrists don’t blindly offer medicines. We do like to see which one works the best for a specific patient but as an industry, we are particular as to who gets the medicine and even in what counts.If the person has slightest tendency to develop suicidal ideation, we limit the number of doses to prevent them from overdosing it.&nbsp;So, I would not agree with the claim that a ‘cocktail of medicines’ led her to psychosis.Although, if the medicines were not taken as instructed, it could have worsened her condition.Reporter: Is there a blind spot for psychiatry?Psychiatrist: Yes absolutely, just like any other area of medicine we cannot fully determine if our patients are following our instructions or not.Medical non-adherence is way more common than one estimates.Particularly in India, we can see patients randomly stopping diabetes pills or hypertension medicines when they start to feel better.So is the case with psychiatric drugs which carry all the more stigma and apprehensions to it.Reporter: Can postpartum psychosis happen to a person of any race or some lie at greater risk?Psychiatrist: Postpartum psychosis can happen to anyone and anywhere. Some underlying mental health conditions like bipolar disorder, depression and even traumatic birth experience can increase one’s risk.However, it is safe to say that the prognosis of mental health disorders in India is relatively better because of the support fabric and interdependency.&nbsp;Postpartum psychosis in IndiaAs per reports, postpartum psychosis is a severe psychiatric disorder that affects about 1 to 2 about every 1000 mothers in India and worldwide.As per reports, a woman named Aswathi was charged with strangling her one year old daughter in Venjaaramodu (Kerala, 2026), allegedly having a belief that her daughter has autism.Likewise, in 2021, another new mother from Kerala’s Kollam had strangled her toddler and allegedly was suffering from mental health conditions.Need for postpartum careLindsay Clancy’s trial has revealed that though rare, conditions like postpartum psychosis can occur to anyone. It also highlights the need to rethink and upgrade postpartum care of a woman who has just given birth.The case has also highlighted the boundary where a guilty mind ends and criminal responsibility begins.

primary_source.headline: Sexual assaults happening almost every day in Ceuta, prosecutors say
primary_source.content: Some 5,000 migrants who entered Ceuta from Morocco are estimated to still be in the Spanish exclave That number meant there was almost one case every day, Ceuta's chief prosecutor Silvia Rojas said. She told El País newspaper migrant girls were "particularly vulnerable because of their irregular status in the territory". At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July and although most have returned, as many as 5,000 remain - leading to unrest in the autonomous city in North Africa and a crisis for Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Between 1,400 and 1,600 of the estimated 5,000 migrants still in Ceuta are children, according to Rojas. Among the suspected attackers are four Moroccans, three Spaniards and a Belgian, Efe news agency reports.

primary_source.headline: Olivia Rodrigo is standing up for the vulnerable. I wish Taylor Swift would do the same | Arwa Mahdawi
primary_source.content: This weekend, Rodrigo raised millions for charities that benefit women and girls, and she has previously been vocal about Gaza and Ice. With free speech increasingly under threat, her peers should take noteDonald Trump, the 80-year-old president of the United States, spent his weekend whining about a lake and posting memes of Donald’s Ducks. While he was busy with his ducks, Olivia Rodrigo, a 23-year-old pop star, spent her weekend trying to Make America Somewhat Decent Again. On Saturday, Rodrigo hosted the inaugural Daisy Chain Fields festival, bringing together female artists to raise money for women-focused non-profits which have had their funding slashed by the Trump administration. The festival raised $10m (£7.4m) which Melinda French Gates matched, bringing the total to $20m.In a perfect world a singer holding a benefit concert for feminist charities wouldn’t be radical stuff. But we don’t live in a perfect world, do we? We live in hell. Trump has successfully bullied US institutions into doing his bidding. Universities have defunded Diversity, Equity and Inclusion programmes, many media outlets have kowtowed to the US’s self-styled king and tech CEOs have jumped into bed with him. Women’s rights are going backwards globally and our civil liberties are under attack. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: 'They made me give my shirt to another actor': 'Mandaadi' actor Soori recounts shocking humiliation by Tamil star

primary_source.headline: 'They made me give my shirt to another actor': 'Mandaadi' actor Soori recounts shocking humiliation by Tamil star
primary_source.content:
Kollywood actor Soori, who started off his career as a comedian and emerged as a leading actor in Tamil cinema, is eagerly awaiting the release of his much-talked-about movie Mandaadi. During the promotions of the movie, the actor looked back on the harsh realities of his early days in the film industry.Opening up about a painful past experience, the actor recalled a heartbreaking moment when a top star replaced him with an actor who had arrived via a reference. Making matters worse, the crew took his personal shirt and gave it to the replacement actor, never bothering to ask his consent or return it.'Is rape end of a woman's life': Swara Bhasker defends letter to Sanjay Leela Bhansali on 'Padmaavat' jauhar scene "I had shot my scenes alongside a major comedian and a leading superstar. I thought it was my big breakthrough. But after reviewing the shot on the monitor, the hero and the director spoke in private, and everything changed in an instant," said Soori.pic.twitter.com/rmzVwlLvB0&mdash; Amuthabharathi Videos (@videos3210) September 1, 2026
 

"They asked me to take off my shirt so the new actor could wear it. My shirt was tossed into the costume vehicle, and I was left standing on set in just a towel wrapped around my waist, searching for my clothes while they filmed the scene with someone else," Soori added.He further looked back on the hardships of his early career. The actor opened up about a defining, vulnerable moment when he was on the verge of his first major break, only for the opportunity to be snatched away under humiliating conditions.        View this post on Instagram            
 Soori also revealed that the incident caused him immense pain and humiliation at the time but became a major turning point. The setback only hardened his determination to make it in the industry purely on merit, rather than relying on favours or connections, he said.Social media is pouring out love for Soori following his raw revelation during the Mandaadi promotions. Fans are celebrating his remarkable journey, hailing his impressive performances in powerhouse films like Garudan, Kottukkaali, and Vetrimaaran’s two-part saga Viduthalai.

stories.primary_headline: Delhi govt seals Maujpur playschool over toddler's assault, finds multiple building norm violations

primary_source.headline: Delhi govt seals Maujpur playschool over toddler's assault, finds multiple building norm violations
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Delhi government has sealed a playschool in northeast Delhi's&nbsp;Maujpur&nbsp;where a three-year-old boy was allegedly physically and sexually assaulted, after an inspection found multiple safety and building norm violations, including blocked emergency exits and a non-functional fire extinguisher.The director of the pre-school and daycare activity centre failed to produce satisfactory replies or the required permissions during the inspection, according to a report prepared by Yamuna Vihar sub-divisional magistrate.3-year-old sexually abused by Delhi school bus driver four times; AAP leader tears into CM Rekha GuptaThe inspection was conducted to check compliance with provisions of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, and the Delhi Fire Service Act, 2007, it stated.Bengaluru: How are parents vetting daycares now?According to the report, the playschool did not have a fire safety certificate, a sanctioned building plan, or a completion or occupancy certificate. Its emergency exit and staircases were blocked; the only fire extinguisher at the premises was non-functional.A borewell was found at the playschool premises, for which no permission was produced. The rooms lacked proper ventilation, while the basement had rooms being used to conduct classes in violation of the Delhi Municipal Act, the report said.The school was also found operating in a residential area while carrying out commercial activity and also ran a kitchen on the first floor using domestic LPG cylinders, it said, adding that the sealing was carried out "to ensure public safety".The action comes days after a three-year-old boy was allegedly subjected to hours of physical abuse inside the playschool.In his complaint, the child's father alleged that CCTV footage showed his son being tied to a chair for nearly three hours, beaten and kicked repeatedly.The father also said that in one instance, a person was seen placing hands on the child's private parts. The allegation is part of the complaint and is being investigated by police.The family claimed that the child has since been struggling to pass stool and urine, and has become traumatised.The child's father said he called the police helpline 112 on August 27 from outside the playschool and entered the premises along with police personnel, following which the child was medically examined.The FIR filed accordingly mentioned swelling on the child's left thigh and a superficial abrasion near his left eye. No other external injury was noted during the examination, following which further medical examination was conducted at the GTB Hospital.A case was registered at Jafrabad police station on August 28 against four people: the director, principal, a teacher and a caretaker of the playschool.The FIR invoked Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act; and Section 12 (sexual assault) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.A caretaker has been arrested in connection with the case. Another woman has been served a notice to join the investigation, police said.Authorities have seized the CCTV footage and are examining it as part of the investigation, they said.

primary_source.headline: Uttar Pradesh firecracker factory blast: Owner arrested after encounter, seven cops suspended

stories.primary_headline: Explained | What is Quishing and how to safeguard yourself from such online fraud

primary_source.headline: Explained | What is Quishing and how to safeguard yourself from such online fraud
primary_source.content: With wider availability of smartphones and computers, billions of people are online to work, consume multimedia content, play games, seek information for school project work, or for research studies.However, this also attracts criminals to prey on naive people, particularly senior citizens and young adults, who are just getting to know the internet and lack awareness of cyber threats. Quick summary - click for full detailsConcise summary of key highlightsExplained | What is Quishing and how to safeguard yourself from such online fraudIn one lineQuishing is a sophisticated QR code phishing scam bypassing email security to steal personal and financial data.Key points• What is QuishingQuishing is a phishing technique using malicious QR codes to redirect victims to compromised websites or download harmful content, bypassing traditional email security filters.• Sophistication levelQuishing is highly sophisticated, evading detection by secure email gateways like Google Gmail and Microsoft Outlook, which often treat QR codes as benign images.• Target demographicsCybercriminals primarily target senior citizens and young adults who are less aware of cyber threats, exploiting their trust and limited internet knowledge.• Primary risksThe ultimate goal of Quishing is to steal sensitive information such as passwords, financial data, Aadhaar card details, phone numbers, and bank credentials.• Prevention measuresUsers should avoid scanning unsolicited QR codes, install apps only from official stores, regularly update devices, and use reputable antivirus software.Key statistics7.4%Quishing as a percentage of malicious email detections in India11.2%JavaScript-based Trojan as a percentage of cyber threats detected30,000Mobile attacks blocked by Kaspersky in Q1 2026Processed with AI. Reviewed by DH Digital Team.Besides the usual phishing techniques such as sending compromised url links on emails and messenger apps, threat actors have come with new technique called QR Code Quishing.67% of India's Gen Z population feels confident online, but lack cybersecurity awareness: ReportAs per ESET's latest H1 2026 Threat Report, QR code phishing (quishing) has emerged as India's second-largest email threat, accounting for nearly 7.4 per cent of all malicious email detections. JavaScript-based Trojan is the top method, with 11.2 per cent of total cyber threat detection. That said, these Trojan malware-laced emails get detected fast if the user has an anti-virus app in the device.However, QR Quishing is growing out to be big new threat. So, what is it?As noted earlier, Quishing is a new type of phishing technique used by cyber criminals to hoodwink naive device owners scan a malicious QR Code and misdirect to a compromised website.This new Qushing technique is very sophisticated and can easily bypass conventional security screening by platforms such as Google Gmail, Microsoft Outlook and others.Regular emails get screened for URLs, which often get detected instantly. However, these QR codes in emails are perceived by many secure email gateways as benign images.Once this stage is passed, users believe it to be making the users vulnerable to specific forms of phishing attacks. QR codes can also be presented to intended victims in some other ways.QR codes can redirect victims to malicious websites or prompt them to download harmful content. Like all other phishing techniques, the ultimate goal is to steal private information, such as passwords, financial data, or personally identifiable information (PII) like Aadhaar card details, phone number, voter ID card number, house address, online bank account IDs and PIN credentials.Here's how to protect yourself from Quishing and other forms of online fraud1) Whenever you receive a call from a person identifying themselves as a police or Income Tax official, a cellular company executive or a bank official stating that your account may get seized, never panic. Just tell them, I will speak to a bank official and just cut the call. Go to the nearest bank branch and clear the doubt2) Regularly change the password of your netbanking account, both on the website and on the phone app3) If you ever receive messages with URL links or QR Codes to third-party app stores or websites or APK files resembling a bank app, ignore them. Never install an APK file shared on WhatsApp or any messenger or social media platform. For 99 per cent of the time, they are risky and potentially come with malware-laced files4) If you ever receive any cash prizes or job offers online, which look way too lucrative to be believable, then be wary of such rewards. They are likely a bait to reveal your personal information voluntarily; don't fall for this trick.5) Always install and download apps from the official Google Play Store, Microsoft Windows Store, and Apple App Store only6) Even if you are downloading from official websites or aforementioned platforms, make it a habit of reading the reviews of the app. The feedback shared by genuine users will let you know if the app is trustworthy or not.7) Ensure the device is fully updated to the latest version of the operating system. Smartphone, tablet and computer makers regularly send security patches along with OS updates to protect your device from such cyber threats8) Also, to be on the safe side, install anti-virus apps by renowned publishers such as Kaspersky, ESET and others. Kaspersky shared that it has blocked nearly 30,000 mobile attacks against consumers in the region during the first three months of 2026.In India, if you fall victim to online fraud, immediately call toll-free 1930. It is run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, and once you share the bank transaction details, they will be able to trace and freeze the mule bank accounts. Ensure you call them within one hour, as there will be a higher chance of blocking the cyber criminals from withdrawing the ill-gotten money.Digital Hygiene Tips: Here's how to safeguard yourself from mobile malware and cyber fraudGet the latest news on new launches, gadget reviews, apps, cybersecurity, and more on personal technology only on DH Tech.

primary_source.headline: Manasi Parekh, who escaped Nepal-Tibet floods by hours, landed on oxygen after a ‘stupid’ mistake
primary_source.content: Actor Manasi Parekh’s experience of Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) during the Kailash Yatra has sparked questions about whether washing hair at high altitude can trigger the condition. Experts clarify that AMS is primarily caused by reduced oxygen availability and rapid ascent, not by washing one’s hair. However, staying wet and cold at high altitudes can increase physical discomfort, fatigue and sleep problems, making acclimatisation more difficult. Travellers should ascend gradually, stay warm and dry, remain hydrated, eat adequately, rest and avoid alcohol and strenuous exercise during early acclimatisation. Symptoms such as worsening headache or nausea, difficulty walking, confusion, extreme drowsiness, breathlessness at rest or a persistent cough require urgent medical attention and descent to a lower altitude. People with heart, lung or other serious medical conditions should also consult a doctor before undertaking high-altitude trips or pilgrimages.

primary_source.content: A grieving couple who have lost their son find a way to a mirror universe where time runs backwards – but the narrative machinery is shonky and distractingThere is something farcical – grotesque, even – about life played in reverse. A child falling into a tree. A sandwich emerging from a mouth, bite by reconstituted bite. A doctor unstitching a wound. The world is strange in any order, but rewind helps us notice – makes the ordinary absurd.Novels that pick a fight with forward momentum tend to harness this absurdity, revel in it. In The Cockroach (2019), Ian McEwan gives us a sneering Brexit fable about political nostalgia. If voters want to turn back the clock, let them. He unleashes “Economic Reversalism”, which sees employees pay for the privilege of work, and every pound sent back to where it came from. In Time’s Arrow (1991), Martin Amis inverts the Holocaust. stories.primary_headline: NCLT bars Subhash Chandra from alienating assets, stays Rs 6.5 crore repayment plan

primary_source.headline: NCLT bars Subhash Chandra from alienating assets, stays Rs 6.5 crore repayment plan
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Insolvency tribunal NCLT on Tuesday barred Essel Group Chairman Subhash Chandra from alienating his assets and stayed an order allowing him to settle claims arising from personal guarantees on group borrowings for about Rs 6.5 crore, against claims of roughly Rs 22,006 crore.A five-member special bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), headed by President Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, said there was no clear majority view on the repayment plan and therefore the order could not be given effect."It is manifest that as per Section 419(5) of the Companies Act, there is no clear majority view capable of being given effect to. Therefore, the order dated August 25, 2026 of the third member, Nilesh Sharma, Member (Judicial) is stayed," the bench said.Subhash Chandra drops mention of Ambani allegations, shifts focus to settling Essel debtThe tribunal also directed that Chandra, the personal guarantor, "shall not alienate any assets whatsoever either directly or indirectly," and issued notices to all parties in the case.The restraint was sought by Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for dissenting creditors including LIC Housing Finance, Canara Bank and Union Bank, who cautioned that the "substratum" of the matter could otherwise be lost.Justice Grewal said the tribunal would hear all parties at length, including Chandra and creditors opposing the repayment plan."We will hear you at length," the bench told Chandra's counsel when he sought to make a brief submission.The five-member bench said the next hearing would be held on September 23.NCLAT CHALLENGEThe dispute has also reached the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT), where dissenting lenders have challenged the repayment plan.A three-member NCLAT bench led by Officiating Chairperson Justice Yogesh Khanna took up the matter on Tuesday following a request from Mehta. The Solicitor General sought a day's time to decide whether the lenders wanted to proceed with the appeal and said he would return to the tribunal on Wednesday.The latest NCLT order follows a long-running split within the tribunal over Chandra's personal insolvency proceedings.An original two-member NCLT bench comprising Ashok Kumar Bhardwaj, Member (Judicial), and Reena Sinha Puri, Member (Technical), delivered dissenting judgments in September 2025. Bhardwaj approved the repayment plan, while Puri rejected it, citing irregularities in the admission of claims and voting.The matter was subsequently referred to a third member, Nilesh Sharma, who on August 25 approved the repayment plan, subject to excluding certain disputed claims and reallocating their share among eligible creditors.The third member's order was then found not to have produced a clear majority when read with the earlier split verdict, prompting a fresh reference to the NCLT president and the constitution of the five-member special bench.Rs 6.5 CRORE RECOVERY AGAINST Rs 22,006 CRORE CLAIMSThe repayment plan would allow creditors to recover only about Rs 6.5 crore from Chandra's personal estate against claims of roughly Rs 22,006 crore - a recovery of a fraction of the claims.Ten banks and lenders supported the proposal, while dissenting creditors including HDFC Bank, LIC Housing Finance and Canara Bank opposed it, arguing that the recovery was negligible. The dissenting lenders represented less than 20 per cent of the voting share.Chandra has disputed the way the Rs 22,006-crore figure has been presented. He says it does not represent money he personally borrowed but claims arising from personal guarantees he provided for loans taken by Essel Group companies.He has put the claims against his personal guarantees at about Rs 3,990 crore, saying the larger figure relates to claims against the underlying corporate borrowers.The NCLT, while approving the settlement last week, had observed that proceeding with bankruptcy against Chandra could result in an even lower recovery for creditors. The tribunal also noted that his estate "comprises very few assets with negligible value".Dissenting lenders have sought greater scrutiny of Chandra's declared net worth, arguing that it was an important basis on which the guarantees were extended. Figures cited by the lenders put his net worth at about Rs 40,600 crore in 2018 and Rs 45,900 crore in 2017, before falling sharply by 2024.Following Tuesday's order, Chandra said in a statement: "We have complete faith and confidence in our judicial system."FROM BUSINESS EMPIRE TO INSOLVENCYChandra was once among India's most prominent business figures, with interests spanning television, packaging, infrastructure and direct-to-home television. He also served as a member of the Rajya Sabha after being elected with the backing of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).His business empire came under severe pressure after the 2018 liquidity crisis triggered by the collapse of infrastructure financier IL&FS. Essel Group companies, which had accumulated substantial debt, struggled to refinance as liquidity tightened.HDFC Bank mulling appeal against NCLT ruling in Subhash Chandra caseMuch of the group's debt was secured against pledged shares. Falling share prices triggered margin calls and further share sales, adding to the pressure on the group. Some businesses were subsequently sold, while others entered insolvency proceedings.The latest proceedings put the spotlight on India's personal-guarantee insolvency framework, under which lenders can seek recovery from promoters who guarantee corporate borrowings.

stories.brief: New Delhi: Insolvency tribunal NCLT on Tuesday barred Essel Group Chairman Subhash Chandra from alienating his assets and stayed an order allowing him to settle claims arising from personal guarantees on group borrowings for about Rs 6.5 crore, against claims of roughly Rs 22,006 crore. A five-member special bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), headed by President Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, said there was no clear majority view on the repayment plan and therefore the order could not be given effect."It is manifest that as per Section 419(5) of the Companies Act, there is no clear majority view capable of being given effect to. stories.primary_headline: Toxic haze from Indonesian forest fires chokes Malaysian Borneo

primary_source.headline: Toxic haze from Indonesian forest fires chokes Malaysian Borneo - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: It is the region’s worst haze episode since 2015, when fires in Indonesia exposed tens of millions of people to toxic smoke and caused more than 500,000 people to suffer respiratory ailments. On Tuesday, six areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous air quality, with readings above 300 on Malaysia’s Air Pollutant Index. Anything above 100 is considered unhealthy. In Kuching, the state capital, the index hit 407, while in Serian, a town close to the Kalimantan border, it hit 408. Mia Emylia Hassan, 33, a mother of two in Kuching, said the smell of smoke was inescapable. “The air here is very thick,” she said. “It smells like smoke, and it’s just white all over.” Visibility from her house, she said, had dropped to about a kilometre, or roughly half a mile. “We have not seen blue sky for over a month,” she said. The haze arrived in early August, shortly after her 10-month-old daughter came home from the hospital after a lung infection. “She’s not healing properly because her lungs are still developing,” Hassan said. “She’s been on medication this whole month, and she has been coughing and vomiting.” Twice, the family has had to rush the infant back to the emergency room because she could not breathe.

stories.primary_headline: We survived the Aberfan disaster as schoolchildren, but were told to never talk about it again

primary_source.headline: We survived the Aberfan disaster as schoolchildren, but were told to never talk about it again
primary_source.content: Janett was the only child on her street to return home from school on the day of the disaster The eight-year-old had recently recovered from pneumonia, but she was determined to go in for the last day before half-term. Shortly after taking her seat at Pantglas Junior School, Janett was buried beneath tonnes of coal slurry from a collapsing tip. It engulfed the classrooms and killed 144 people, including 116 children. Sixty years later, Janett is one of the many survivors of the Aberfan disaster whose lives were shaped by what they experienced. "I've always wanted to do something to pay back to the community because I think I owed something to the community, because I lived," she said. Janett (front row, second left) with her nursery classmates in 1964. Many of the children in this photograph died in the disaster, two years later

stories.primary_headline: Palestinian farmers rebuild what Israeli settlers destroy in West Bank

primary_source.headline: Palestinian farmers rebuild what Israeli settlers destroy in West Bank - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Along with roughly two dozen other farmers, Najjar is a member of Burin’s Land and Farming Cooperative. They know that they don’t have the capability to fight back against Israel’s military might with arms so instead focus on the land and keeping their connection to it. On July 13, a settler tried to graze his flock inside one of the cooperative’s five greenhouses. Cooperative members struggled to keep the livestock away until Israeli border police arrived. Najjar recalled challenging the officers over why a settler had been permitted onto land the army itself had designated a closed military zone, from which Israeli citizens are, on paper, also barred. The settler left angry. In Arabic, he told Najjar: “You’ll see.” The next night, roughly 10 settlers arrived, gutting all five of the cooperative’s greenhouses, cutting away their plastic sheeting and destroying their irrigation networks. The damage, by the cooperative’s estimate, ran to roughly 30,000 shekels (about $10,000) in plastic sheeting alone. About 9,000 tomato seedlings worth 8,000 shekels ($2,670) had been bought that same morning for planting. They died within hours because there was nowhere else to put them. For a cooperative that pools land, labour and produce among about 25 families, the loss reverberated beyond the five greenhouses themselves. “We’re talking about 25 families working inside the cooperative,” Najjar said. “This year is the most difficult year for the cooperative. We’re facing many attacks by the settlers and the army.”

stories.primary_headline: Two dead and about 15 people missing after flash flood in Grand Canyon

primary_source.headline: Two dead and about 15 people missing after flash flood in Grand Canyon - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: At least two people have been confirmed to have been killed and about 15 people remain missing after a major flash flood hit the Grand Canyon in the US state of Arizona, authorities said. The National Park Service (NPS) reported on Monday that a second body has been recovered as the search continued. The body of a 46-year-old man was recovered on Sunday evening near Crystal Rapids along the Colorado River, the park service said earlier, without providing additional details. The flooding in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the Colorado River, wiped out footbridges over the creek and significantly altered the landscape, widening the creek bed and creating what appeared to be a new river rapid. Popular tourist spots, including the Bright Angel Campground, Phantom Ranch and parts of the North Kaibab Trail, remained closed on Sunday while park officials surveyed the damage, the park said. Rafting trips on the Colorado River also have been halted for now. Parth Desai was hiking through a narrow passage in Bright Angel Canyon with a group of fellow doctors and a park ranger when the downpour started. “We saw the creek flood, waterfalls coming up out of nowhere; boulders, mud, landslides happening everywhere,” he told The Associated Press news agency.

stories.primary_headline: Think twice before installing this device promising free movies

primary_source.headline: Think twice before installing this device promising free movies
primary_source.content:
As online services get better at blocking malicious traffic, the attackers and scammers behind them have been forced to find new ways to reach their targets. The alternative of choice is now what are known as residential proxy networks. These systems funnel millions of home Internet connections into a unified network, and the proxy operators allow attackers to route their malicious traffic through these connections for a fee. The online services see only IP addresses with good reputations and geolocations that don’t stand out.
More often than not, the home users have no idea that their connections are being used to facilitate crime and occasionally even nation-state attacks. Users who do know often don’t care much. In exchange for leasing out part of their unlimited bandwidth to others, many get free movie and TV show streaming. Several less tech-savvy people I know who own such digital media players have told me, after I explain how the media players piggyback off their connections, that the bonanza of content is worth it. They find the tangible benefits outweigh the abstract harm they pose.
Infecting already compromised devices
Research published Monday brings the threat into much clearer view. Security firm Plume cataloged a vast ecosystem of malware that preys squarely on users of SuperBox, just one of many media players offering pirated content. These malicious apps can be surreptitiously installed by remote attackers even when the devices are positioned behind a router. While Monday’s deep-dive analysis focused exclusively on SuperBox, Plume warned that dozens of similar streaming devices pose precisely the same threat.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: NASA's next "great observatory" begins mission to widen our view of the Universe

primary_source.headline: NASA's next "great observatory" begins mission to widen our view of the Universe
primary_source.content:
NASA's $4.3 billion Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, equipped with a 300-megapixel camera sighted through a refurbished spy mirror, launched Sunday from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on a mission to reveal the mysterious forces driving the Universe.
The new mission will extend the vision of NASA's other famous observatories, providing a field of view 100 times wider than the Hubble Space Telescope and complementing the groundbreaking work of the James Webb Space Telescope. Roman is just the second NASA-led astrophysics mission to launch this century, following the launch of Webb in 2021.
Unlike Webb, which suffered many years of delays before reaching space, Roman arrived at the launch pad nine months before NASA's commitment to send it skyward by May 2027.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: UAE intercepts drone after US and Iran exchange attacks

primary_source.headline: UAE intercepts drone after US and Iran exchange attacks - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The United Arab Emirates says it has engaged a drone coming from Iran over its waters and denied reports of an attack on its Al Menhad airbase, after the United States and Iran resumed hostilities for the first time since July. Iran’s army said in a statement cited by Iranian news agencies that dozens of drones were launched at US military assets at the Al Menhad airbase in the UAE early on Monday. In a statement on X on Monday, the UAE’s Ministry of Defence described the reports as “false” and “urged the public to rely on official sources for information and to refrain from circulating rumours or inaccurate information”. Later, the ministry said the UAE’s air force intercepted a drone “over the country’s territorial waters, approaching from Iran”. The incident comes after the US and Iran exchanged attacks overnight, further denting hopes for a resolution of the more than six-month-long conflict. US forces on Sunday struck two Iranian launchers on Iran’s Larak Island, some 660km (410 miles) east of ⁠Kharg Island, a US official said. Iran retaliated by attacking two bases used by US forces in Jordan and the UAE’s Al Menhad airbase, according to Iranian media.

stories.primary_headline: Russia, China leaders to meet at Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit

primary_source.headline: Russia, China leaders to meet at Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Russia’s Vladimir Putin, China’s Xi Jinping and more than a dozen other leaders are set to gather in Kyrgyzstan on Monday for the annual summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has historically focused on economic issues, but President Putin and President Xi have also used the summit to promote their vision of a multipolar world and to present a united front against the West. The SCO’s founding declaration says the group is “not an alliance directed against other states”. However, at last year’s gathering, Putin accused Western countries of provoking the Ukraine war, while Xi denounced “acts of intimidation”, referring to US-Chinese tensions. Also expected to be in attendance are Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and his Turkish counterpart Recep Tayyip Erdogan, though Turkiye is not a member of the organisation. Pezeshkian is expected to hold bilateral talks with Putin at this year’s SCO in the Kyrgyz capital of Bishkek. The foreign ministers of both countries met in July during the SCO’s Council of Foreign Ministers meeting. Iran joined the bloc in 2023 and maintains close military ties to Russia and energy links with China.

stories.primary_headline: Investigators probe cause of Northern Cyprus boat capsizing, crew detained

primary_source.headline: Investigators probe cause of Northern Cyprus boat capsizing, crew detained - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Police have detained the captain and seven crew members of a ferry that capsized off Northern Cyprus, killing at least eight of the 270 people on board and leaving 18 others missing. The transport minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Erhan Arikli, told Turkish news agency Anadolu on Sunday that passengers had made several allegations involving the crew, including that the doors had been locked and that the captain fled the vessel. Others said the vessel began taking on water shortly after leaving the port and that crew members had failed to heed their warnings. Arikli said his ministry would launch an investigation separate from the police probe. Al Jazeera correspondent Resul Serdar said that finding those missing at sea was the priority and that “a huge deployment to the area as part of the search and rescue effort affiliated with the Northern Cyprus coastguard command” had begun. The coastguard has deployed passenger ships, five pilotage units and two helicopters. Turkish naval forces assigned another six naval units.

primary_source.headline: One person killed, five wounded in shooting at rave in Switzerland - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: An Italian woman has been killed and five people have been injured in a shooting at an overnight rave in northern Switzerland, police say. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni named the victim as Maria Spinelli on social media. Swiss President Guy Parmelin wrote in a post on X that he was saddened by the incident early on Sunday and shared his condolences “to the family and relatives of the young victim”. “A 22-year-old woman died of her injuries at the scene. Four men and one woman, aged between 24 and 27, were taken to hospital. They are suffering from injuries ranging from minor to serious,” police said on social media. “Searches to find the perpetrators, who are currently unknown, are under way,” the police report said, adding that the motives and exact circumstances regarding the incident in Aarau, north of Zurich, were not yet known. Contacted by the AFP news agency, police were unable to say how many suspects there were or the type of firearms used in the shooting. The Swiss newspaper Blick reported that the shots were fired before 3am (01:00 GMT) on the sidelines of the Aarauer Rave.

stories.primary_headline: Pogacar to have surgery on broken collarbone after horrific Vuelta crash

primary_source.headline: Pogacar to have surgery on broken collarbone after horrific Vuelta crash - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar was sent hurtling head-over-handlebars in a frightening crash that forced him to pull out of the Spanish Vuelta. The Slovenian suffered a concussion and broke two bones, one of which will require surgery, after he appeared to lose control when a stone rolled across the road on Saturday. “Tadej has been diagnosed with a concussion, displaced left clavicle fracture, a stable C7 cervical fracture, and multiple abrasions,” said UAE Team Emirates medical director Adrian Rotunno. “Fortunately, no other major injuries and no neurological fallout. He will require clavicle surgery, which will be delayed due to concussion precautions. Tadej remains under the care of our medical team and we’ll provide further updates following the surgery,” Rotunno added. Pogacar held a big lead in the Vuelta and was heavily favoured to win the title to complete a hat-trick of cycling’s three Grand Tours. But he crashed about 33km from the finish of the eighth stage. He tried to get back on his bike but could not carry on and walked to an ambulance. Race organisers confirmed he pulled out of the race. TV video showed Pogacar with cuts on his head, left arm and shoulder. He swerved to his right into other cyclists as he appeared to try to avoid something in the road. The Tour de France champion lost control and flew over his handlebars, hitting his head and shoulder.

stories.primary_headline: Mapping Iran war’s strikes on Gulf energy and its impact on future of oil

primary_source.headline: Mapping Iran war’s strikes on Gulf energy and its impact on future of oil - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Six months into the war on Iran, the largest US oil companies have posted their biggest profits since 2022, selling less oil at far higher prices. But the conflict is also putting their longstanding Gulf investments at risk, exposing the industry’s uneasy balance between wartime gains and mounting geopolitical vulnerability for investors worldwide. Since the war began on February 28, Brent crude has risen about 22 percent, from $72 to $88 a barrel. In the absence of a lasting resolution, the disruption is likely to continue supporting higher energy prices and creating windfalls for producers, despite placing energy companies’ regional assets and future projects at greater risk. Rahul Choudhary, vice president of Upstream Research at Rystad Energy, an independent energy research company, said the conflict has already reduced the amount of oil and gas US energy firms are drawing from the Gulf region. “Overall we expect US companies’ share of gas supplies [from the region] to fall by around 40 percent this year compared to last year [and] the share of oil supplies to drop by 30-35 percent,” he told Al Jazeera. While higher commodity prices have helped offset the immediate financial impact, Choudhary said prolonged disruption is likely to delay major projects and weigh on the future growth plans of US oil and gas companies with a presence in the region.

stories.primary_headline: Haitian gangs release 13 captives after mass kidnapping in Kenscoff

primary_source.headline: Haitian gangs release 13 captives after mass kidnapping in Kenscoff - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The United Nations has announced that six children and seven women kidnapped last week in the hillside community of Kenscoff, Haiti, have been released. In a statement late on Friday, representatives from the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) used the news to call attention to the ongoing crisis unfolding in Haiti — and the toll it has taken on the country’s youth. “This release offers a rare moment of hope amid the violence threatening children in Haiti,” said Yannig Dussart, the group’s deputy representative in Haiti. “The Kenscoff abduction was not an isolated incident but another stark reminder of the scale and frequency of attacks on children across the country.” The freed captives were part of one of the largest mass abductions in recent memory in Haiti. On the night of August 23, an estimated 150 armed gang members are believed to have attacked Kenscoff, which sits on the hillsides overlooking the capital Port-au-Prince and the suburb of Petionville.

stories.primary_headline: Turkiye summons Ukraine ambassador over Black Sea attacks

primary_source.headline: Turkiye summons Ukraine ambassador over Black Sea attacks - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Ukraine’s ambassador to Turkiye has been summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Ankara following two attacks on Turkish-operated vessels in the Black Sea. The Lider Kocatepe was also targeted by a drone when on its way to assist the Lider Bordo Mavi the next day. Turkish media reported that the Lider Bordo Mavi was towed to the Turkish port of Samsun. Turkiye has been calling for a halt to attacks on civilian vessels in the Black Sea as Ukraine and Russia continue to target each other’s export revenues. Navigating the sea has carried heightened risk ever since Russia launched its war on Ukraine in February 2022, but attacks there have escalated.

stories.primary_headline: Sequoia-incubated Empirik launches with $21M to predict outages before they happen

primary_source.headline: Sequoia-incubated Empirik launches with $21M to predict outages before they happen
primary_source.content: Empirik announced Tuesday that it is spinning out as an independent company after raising $21 million in seed funding from Sequoia, Canapi, and Alumni Ventures. By serving as an autonomous infrastructure engineer, Empirik allows busy DevOps and site reliability engineering teams to offload routine troubleshooting and focus on higher-value priorities. Since launching earlier this year, Empirik has already brought on customers ranging from startups to several Fortune 500 players, including S&P Global, Guardant Health, and a major consumer packaged goods (CPG) company. Empirik’s goal is to do for infrastructure engineers what Cursor and Claude Code did for software developers: automate certain tasks so they can work significantly faster. As AI accelerates the pace of software development, tools that help infrastructure engineers keep up with constant system changes are more vital than ever, Chandrayana told TechCrunch. “What agentic AI did for software, Empirik wants to do for infrastructure engineering,” he added.

stories.primary_headline: India’s ER&D services revenue projected to cross $100 billion in revenue by 2030: Nasscom

primary_source.headline: India’s ER&D services revenue projected to cross $100 billion in revenue by 2030: Nasscom
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: Artificial intelligence is moving to the core of engineering research and development (ER&D), reshaping how products are designed, tested and operated.&nbsp;As products become more software-defined and data-driven, Indian ER&D firms have a chance to move beyond execution and take full lifecycle ownership of global product development, Nasscom said.&nbsp;A large part of this growth will be driven by AI moving beyond productivity tools to getting embedded across the engineering lifecycle - from design and simulation to manufacturing and operations. Dubai Chambers signs MoU with Nasscom, FKCCINasscom flagged Physical AI as the next frontier. In a report titled 'Physical AI - Redefining ER&D opportunity for India', the industry body said demand will unfold in three waves. First, intelligent products and operations - embedded AI, connected equipment, predictive maintenance and intelligent inspection - will scale as enterprises retrofit AI into existing systems. Second, simulation, virtual engineering and intelligent manufacturing will gain as firms move from pilots to production.Over the longer term, autonomous systems could become the largest opportunity once challenges around safety, reliability and real-world deployment are addressed. India is well placed to become the engineering layer that connects AI with the physical world, Nasscom said, given its strength in AI, embedded systems, automotive and industrial R&D, simulation and data engineering. The shift also opens new commercial models beyond traditional services, including AI-as-a-Service, Robotics-as-a-Service, leasing, autonomous platforms and agentic deployments."India's ER&D growth will be shaped by how effectively we combine our engineering depth with AI to take on greater ownership of global product development. Physical AI adds an important new dimension to this opportunity," said Rajesh Nambiar, President, Nasscom. Realising this will need cross-disciplinary talent, platform and ecosystem partnerships, and domain-specific models that turn real-world data into continuously improving systems, the report said.

primary_source.headline: H D Kumaraswamy urges auto industry to keep growth broad-based, focus on Indian customers
primary_source.content: Union Heavy Industries Minister H D Kumaraswamy Tuesday called on the country’s automobile industry to ensure its expansion remains broad-based so that the benefits of manufacturing reach ordinary households, with the Indian customer placed at the centre of every decision.Addressing the annual conclave of the Federation of Automobile Dealers Association (FADA), the minister for Heavy Industries and Steel said manufacturing must form the core of India’s economic growth as the nation advances towards Viksit Bharat 2047.“But manufacturing alone does not build a nation’s prosperity. It must reach the household. Let us keep the growth broad-based, keep the transition human and keep the Indian customer at the centre of every decision we take,” he said.'Automobile Hub of India': Why has Chakan emerged as Maharashtra’s big political issue?Kumaraswamy underlined the government’s push to promote electric mobility and strengthen domestic manufacturing in the automobile and auto components sectors.He noted that the PM E-DRIVE scheme, launched under the leadership of the Prime Minister Narendra Modi with an outlay of Rs 10,900 crore, has already supported the sale of more than 26.5 lakh electric vehicles.The minister also highlighted the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for automobiles and auto components, which has an outlay of Rs 25,038 crore. The scheme has 82 approved applicants, has attracted cumulative investment of over Rs 44,036 crore and has generated close to 68,000 jobs, he said.

primary_source.headline: KPSC 'scam': CID probes Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, Basavaraj Kannale as key suspects
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: The investigation by the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) into the alleged irregularities at the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) centres around IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar and Basavaraj Kannale as the key suspects, well-placed sources said. The two are currently being interrogated by CID, as a court granted the probe team their custody for 10 days on Monday. KPSC 'scam': IAS officer Gyanendra Gangwar, 'mastermind' Basavaraj Kannale sent to CID custodyIt is suspected that Kannale, the alleged mastermind and a Tumkur University syndicate member, who is also linked with the state BJP, facilitated the leaks and tampering of OMR sheets through Gangwar. CID is also probing allegations that candidates were approached by middlemen and paid Rs 40 lakhs in advance to secure the postings. This was alleged in the FIR registered at the Vidhana Soudha police station in July. The FIR listed 29 such candidates.Sources said that carbon dating and forensic analysis are expected to be conducted to ascertain if the OMR sheets were tampered with and whether the CCTV feed was destroyed. CID is also expected to scour the bank accounts of the arrested suspects and the suspected candidates to establish a money trail. A team of officials had previously searched Kannale’s premises in Bengaluru's Sanjay Nagar. Kannale’s photographs with several BJP politicians in the state had gone viral on Monday. Kannale operated several businesses, including tours and travels, and was in constant contact with Gangwar, sources said. KPSC, which conducts competitive exams for government jobs in Karnataka, is facing scrutiny over allegations of irregularities in the final selection process for the Veterinary Officers’ Recruitment Exam.KPSC ‘scam’: CID detains IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar GangwarJD(S) workers detainedWorkers of JD(S) and some leaders were detained by the police on Tuesday after they tried to storm the Congress office. They were demanding a CBI probe into the KPSC irregularities. When the protesters tried to storm the KPCC building, the police detained them, took them into preventive custody and released them later.

primary_source.headline: District level tenders to be invited for Indira food kit for Anna Bhagya beneficiaries
primary_source.content: Mangaluru:&nbsp; Guarantee Implementation Authority Chairman H M Revanna said that an Indira Food Kit containing tur dal, sugar, salt and edible oil would soon be distributed to beneficiaries under the Anna Bhagya scheme. District-level tenders will be invited to supply the kits through the public distribution system (PDS).Speaking to mediapersons, Revanna said the initiative would help prevent the pilferage and diversion of free rice to the black market. “It will ensure that nutritious food reaches the beneficiaries,” he said.Initially, the government had planned to invite a state-level tender for supplying the kits. However, it later decided to conduct the tender process at the district level.Udupi: Police seize lorry illegally transporting Anna Bhagya rice to Kerala He said the Rs 2,000 monthly financial assistance under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme was not credited to beneficiaries’ accounts for February and March as the funds had not been released from the treasury. However, he denied allegations by the Opposition that the funds had been misused. “The government has promised that the amount will be released to the beneficiaries’ accounts shortly,” he said.He added that the re-verification of Gruha Lakshmi beneficiaries would be taken up shortly through six-member committees at the gram panchayat and ward levels. The committees are expected to be constituted within the next 10 days.Revanna said Rs 117 crore had been credited to the bank accounts of deceased beneficiaries under the Gruha Lakshmi scheme across the state. Of this, Rs 30 crore had already been recovered. In Dakshina Kannada, Rs 3.34 crore had been credited to the accounts of deceased beneficiaries, of which Rs 1.60 crore had been recovered so far, he said.To a query, he said that five guarantee schemes will be continued even in 2028 as the schemes have benefited the people in the state. stories.primary_headline: At $1 billion, Happiest Minds-ITC Infotech eyes bigger deals via cross-sell

primary_source.headline: At $1 billion, Happiest Minds-ITC Infotech eyes bigger deals via cross-sell
primary_source.content: Bengaluru: With foundational AI and speciality consulting firms growing big, Indian IT services players who have created a niche will have to become bigger, and the only way to do that is through consolidation."Consolidation is the way forward for customers, the company, and employees. It makes sense for all stakeholders," Happiest Minds senior executives said on Tuesday.On Monday, the mid-tier IT services firm announced its merger with ITC Infotech and promoter Ashok Soota and his promoter group are selling a 22.1 per cet stake in the company for Rs 1,330 crore. Speaking at a press conference, Venkatraman Narayanan, Managing Director, Happiest Minds, said, "With entry barriers going up and the need for scale to invest in AI and platforms, consolidation is the way forward." ITC Infotech to acquire 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds for Rs 1,330 croreIT services firms are focusing more on mergers and acquisitions, as recently Coforge acquired Silicon-based AI-native firm Encora for an enterprise value of about Rs 21,100 crore. The company also recently announced the successful closure of its acquisition of Cigniti Technologies. TCS announced the acquisition of sports car manufacturer Porsche's management and IT consultancy subsidiary MHP for over Rs 3,574 crore.Persistent Systems' Euro 1.27 billion all-cash acquisition of Munich-headquartered digital engineering company Nagarro will boost the former's European expansion plans. In 2022, Larsen & Toubro (L&T) announced the merger of its group companies - L&T Infotech and Mindtree. Companies are looking at cross-selling, and they are hoping that they could win many large deals.Joseph Anantharaju, Co-chairman & CEO, Happiest Minds, said, "Now we can offer customers a one-stop shop for large TCV deals. It allows us to bid for bigger deals." The management said Soota has been looking to reduce his holding in Happiest Minds for some time to raise capital for Happiest Health and SKAN, a non-profit organisation focusing on ageing and neurological research. Post-merger, Soota will hold 7.55 per cent in the combined entity as an ordinary shareholder. SKAN, which recently opened its first campus, also plans to scale to a 2-lakh sq ft facility that requires about Rs 350 crore capex.KKR to acquire minority stake in BookMyShowAnantharaju said the industry is going through a shift with AI becoming central, increasing focus on business outcomes, vendor consolidation and need for broader capabilities and execution scale. Happiest Minds is strong in AI, digital product engineering, cloud, data and cyber security, while ITC Infotech brings complementary strengths in enterprise applications and deep domain expertise in CPG, retail, manufacturing and travel and hospitality.When asked about leadership changes, he said there will be no leadership change or employee rationalisation, with ITC requesting all Happiest Minds leaders to continue. Anantharaju said he has committed to continue. "We are not looking at any rationalisation of headcount. In fact, we need more people," he added.Industry experts see this merger as an overall good business combination of companies that bring diverse skills across digital engineering, data and enterprise technologies. Praveen Bhadada, CEO & Managing Director, NeoNay Global, a consulting firm, said while both platforms had grown reasonably well in the last 5 years, scale is decisive in the current environment."Clients are consolidating vendor panels, AI adoption demands front-loaded investment, and deal sizes are shrinking due to AI-led compression. A sub-$500-million company simply cannot absorb these pressures. At $1 billion, the combined entity becomes India's 11th-largest listed IT services player and enters a bracket where it can sustain multi-vertical, multi-geography delivery without concentration risk," he said.UnearthInsight said the two businesses are complementary rather than overlapping. Happiest Minds brings faster growth, a richer digital engineering mix and stronger adjusted PAT density, while ITC Infotech brings scale, enterprise relationships and a more balanced run-services base.Their revenue productivity is also broadly similar, at roughly Rs 36 lakh per employee, suggesting that the combination is adding capabilities and market access rather than simply diluting operating productivity.However, Bhadada said the challenge will be to effectively integrate the two companies, expand AI-led capabilities faster than the peer set and protect the existing base of clients and revenue. stories.primary_headline: Centre halves sugar stock limit for dealers to curb high prices

primary_source.headline: Centre halves sugar stock limit for dealers to curb high prices
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Centre on Tuesday further tightened stock-holding norms for sugar dealers, slashing the limit from 4,000 quintals to 2,000 quintals with effect from September 15 to November 30, in a bid to rein in high retail prices of the sweetener.The food ministry said the earlier limit of 4,000 quintals, imposed on August 1, will continue to apply in Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas, “considering the specific market requirements of the region.” Under the amended rules, no dealer can hold any stock for more than 30 days from the date of receipt or exceed 2,000 quintals of sugar at any time anywhere in the country.Faulty sugar estimates leave a bitter tasteThe ministry said the move is intended to ensure adequate availability of sugar in the domestic market and to check hoarding and speculative trading. It explained that Kolkata sources sugar from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra and supplies it onward to the eastern and north-eastern states, which is why the higher limit has been retained there.The decision comes even as retail prices remain high. The all-India average retail price stood at Rs 63.28 per kg on August 31, up 37 per cent from Rs 46.02 a year earlier, according to Consumer Affairs Ministry data. Wholesale prices rose 36.28 per cent year-on-year to Rs 58.40 per kg.Karnataka: Hike in sugar prices forces teachers to pay out-of-pocketIndustry data, however, points to some cooling at the mill gate. The ex-mill price of sugar in Maharashtra fell about 30 per cent to Rs 45-46 per kg on September 1 from a peak of Rs 67 per kg on August 18.The Centre has blamed mills for “jacking up” prices and maintains that the country has adequate stocks. This is despite production estimates for the 2025-26 marketing year (October-September) being revised downward to 306 lakh tonnes from an earlier projection of 343 lakh tonnes. Annual domestic demand is estimated at around 280-285 lakh tonnes.
