stories.primary_headline: Centre for security threats among key decisions as India highlights 13 outcomes from SCO summit

primary_source.headline: Centre for security threats among key decisions as India highlights 13 outcomes from SCO summit
primary_source.content:
Bishkek: India on Tuesday highlighted several key outcomes from the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit, including measures to strengthen cooperation on security and tackle transnational threats such as terrorism and extremism.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) listed 13 outcomes, one of which was the approval of regulations for a "Universal Centre for Countering Challenges and Threats to the Security of SCO Member States".The centre is expected to strengthen cooperation among SCO members in tackling terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats, and enable better coordination and information sharing, the MEA said in a post on X.SCO must work unitedly to dismantle terror ecosystem: PM ModiThe security-related decision assumes significance as Prime Minister Narendra Modi -- addressing the summit in the presence of Pakistani counterpart Shehbaz Sharif, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders -- called on the grouping to confront countries using terrorism as an "instrument of state policy".The prime minister urged the SCO to work unitedly to "dismantle the entire ecosystem" of terrorist financing, recruitment, radicalisation and safe havens and reject "double standards" in the fight against terrorism -- remarks widely viewed as a direct swipe at Pakistan.pic.twitter.com/JkQiZCIedP&mdash; Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) September 1, 2026
 

"We must send a strong message to countries that use terrorism as an instrument of policy and provide safe haven and support to terrorists that terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone," Modi said.Among the outcomes highlighted by the MEA is the Bishkek Declaration, which is expected to provide India a platform to articulate its positions on regional security, development and connectivity, and strengthen its engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.Another outcome is a protocol on amendments and additions to the SCO Charter, which enables India to participate in shaping the grouping's evolving institutional framework and supports the inclusion of English within the SCO framework.The SCO is a political, economic and security grouping founded in 2001 by China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. It has since expanded to include India, Pakistan, Iran and Belarus as full members, with several other countries holding observer or dialogue-partner status.The SCO framework is essentially a permanent Eurasian intergovernmental and regional cooperation organisation focused on security, counter-terrorism, and economic and political collaborations.The grouping marked its 25th anniversary this year, with the summit held in Bishkek under Kyrgyzstan’s chairmanship.The MEA on Tuesday also highlighted a decision approving regulations for the executive committee of the SCO Anti-Narcotics Centre, which would facilitate closer coordination among member states against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.At SCO Summit, Pakistan PM Sharif says water must never be weaponisedA programme on combating drug addiction and another on the proliferation of synthetic drugs and their precursors, which would run up to 2030, were also among the 13 outcomes.The first programme seeks to facilitate exchange of best practices in prevention, treatment and rehabilitation, while the second aims to improve information-sharing and operational coordination among enforcement agencies.The MEA also listed statements on cooperation in energy conservation and energy efficiency, and on the development of energy systems.These provide scope for exchange of technology, experience and best practices and cooperation in modernising and strengthening the resilience of energy systems, MEA said.An SCO statement on providing assistance to states affected by emergencies was also highlighted. It provides for sharing of expertise and capacity-building in disaster management and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, it said.Another protocol seeks to amend the 2010 agreement on cooperation among SCO governments in combating crime. The amendment is aimed at strengthening coordination among law-enforcement agencies against organised and cross-border crime.The MEA also highlighted a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on cooperation in combating climate change, which provides a platform for cooperation on climate adaptation and mitigation, climate-resilient development and technology.An MoU between authorised agencies of SCO member states on cooperation in the field of information was also among the outcomes. It is aimed at promoting institutional exchanges and wider dissemination of India's perspectives and initiatives within the SCO information space.An MoU on cooperation in the field of artificial intelligence was the final outcome highlighted by the MEA. It provides scope for India to share its digital and AI experience, promote responsible and inclusive use of AI and expand technology and innovation partnerships within the SCO, the ministry said.

stories.primary_headline: 'My best film yet': Emraan Hashmi on 'Awarapan 2' success

primary_source.headline: 'My best film yet': Emraan Hashmi on 'Awarapan 2' success
primary_source.content:
Riding high on the success of his latest release, Awarapan 2, actor Emraan Hashmi has called the action-emotional thriller his "best film yet." Talking about the journey of reviving the iconic character Shivam Pandit nearly two decades after the original, Emraan credited producer Vishesh Bhatt’s relentless persistence and vision for breathing new life into the franchise.The sequel, which released in theaters on August 14, 2026, has turned into a major box office juggernaut, minting over Rs 200 crore globally. For Emraan, the success represents personal redemption for the 2007 cult classic Awarapan, which gained massive popularity on home video and television over the years despite performing averagely during its initial theatrical release.'Awarapan 2' Box Office: Emraan Hashmi starrer crosses Rs 128 crore on Day 7, eyes big second weekendLooking back on the film’s warm reception, Emraan wrote on Instagram:"I’ve always held Shivam Pandit very close to my heart. When Vishesh came to me with the idea for Awarapan 2, I was hesitant because sequels to beloved cult films carry huge expectations. But Vishesh had a singular, clear vision—he didn't just want to make a cash grab; he wanted to give Shivam the emotional closure and grand scale he deserved. Looking at how audiences have embraced the film, I can confidently say it’s my best work to date."        View this post on Instagram            
 Emraan concluded his note with an appeal to audiences. He urged viewers to experience Awarapan 2 on the big screen: “Feel the emotional roller coaster. Let the music take over. And celebrate it the way it was meant to be celebrated - a big screen, big sound cinematic experience.”Earlier, producer Vishesh Bhatt revealed that convincing Emraan to step back into the role took time, as the actor was initially cautious about revisiting the broken anti-hero nearly 19 years later."Emraan and I both carried the heartache of Awarapan not getting its financial due back in 2007," Vishesh Bhatt shared.        View this post on Instagram            
 'Awarapan 2' movie review: When nostalgia isn't enoughFrom Emraan Hashmi to Ajay Devgn: When Bollywood’s villains were broken men, not killing machines "There was a strong spiritual core to Shivam’s character that felt incomplete. I knew we had to honour those silences and emotional depth while adapting to modern cinema standards. Once Emraan saw the script by Bilal Siddiqui and Nitin Kakkar, everything clicked," he added.Directed by Nitin Kakkar, Awarapan 2 follows an older, retired Shivam Pandit who is drawn out of isolation and into Bangkok’s dangerous underbelly to bust a child trafficking network. stories.primary_headline: Supreme Court questions Shiv Sena corporator over attack on Kalyan doctors, flags bail concerns

primary_source.headline: Supreme Court questions Shiv Sena corporator over attack on Kalyan doctors, flags bail concerns
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday came down heavily on Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Sukrya Mhatre for the alleged assault on doctors at Shastrinagar Hospital in Kalyan, observing that attacks on medical professionals inside hospitals could not be treated lightly and indicating it was inclined to uphold the Bombay High Court’s stay on his bail.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Augustine George Masih was hearing Mhatre’s challenge to the High Court’s July 18 order staying the bail granted to him by a Kalyan magistrate and its August 7 order imposing stringent conditions.&nbsp;Supreme Court quashes FIRs on NEET protesters nationwide, bars fresh casesThe High Court had initiated suo motu proceedings after the magistrate granted bail to Mhatre and his associates.“This is a case where you should have been put in detention. Medical personnel are threatened like this, who will come to the aid of people at large? Absolutely not justified. This kind of people don’t deserve it,” the bench remarked.The court also noted that Mhatre was caught on video and that the footage had gone viral. It emphasised the trauma caused when a mob attacks inside a hospital.Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Mhatre, argued that the High Court erred in taking suo motu cognisance and staying the bail order without giving him a hearing, including through a special Saturday sitting.&nbsp;He also questioned the High Court’s directions on completing investigation, filing the chargesheet and framing charges within fixed timelines.The Supreme Court rejected these submissions, holding that the High Court was fully justified in intervening.&nbsp;“You are a public elected person,” the bench observed. It indicated it found no fault with the July 18 stay order.Advocate Siddharth Dharmadhikari, representing the State of Maharashtra, informed the court that the state would file a special leave petition the same day challenging the High Court’s August 7 order that had granted bail to Mhatre with conditions.&nbsp;The Indian Medical Association also intervened to oppose bail.The bench directed that the state’s challenge, once filed, be listed along with Mhatre’s petition on Monday.The case arose from a July 6 incident involving a nine-month pregnant woman allegedly kept waiting at the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation-run hospital. An FIR was registered the next day naming Mhatre as the prime accused. A magistrate granted him bail on July 14, which the High Court stayed on July 18 amid doctors’ protests.

stories.primary_headline: Smart ideas for preserving summer fruit | Kitchen aide

primary_source.headline: Smart ideas for preserving summer fruit | Kitchen aide
primary_source.content:
From fermenting plums in honey and pickling courgettes in vinegar brine to a British take on kimchi, there are many ways to make the most of the warm-weather harvestWhat’s the best way to preserve late-summer fruit and veg?Jess, by email
 Fruit, fruit everywhere, so try fermenting it in honey, says Rachel de Thample, author of The Fermentation Year (published in September). “I’m currently looking at a jar of blackberries, but whole plums would be gorgeous, too,” she says, especially when eaten with blue cheese – “or any cheese, really” – meat or fish; you can also use the syrup like maple syrup or cordial. De Thample packs the fruit into sterilised jars and pours in just enough honey to cover it: “If the fruit has a low acidity, add a spoonful of lemon juice or a splash of cider vinegar as well.” Pop on the lid and leave for a few weeks. “It gets fizzy, but it doesn’t get to that explosive stage, because it has quite a concentrated sugar content. It’ll keep for up to a year at room temperature, but I normally pop it in the fridge after a few weeks.”Kimchi is another option to keep Jess enjoying summer fruits all year round. “In Korea, apples and pears are traditional, but there’s a kimchi for every season and region,” says De Thample, who takes a British approach with a courgette, blackcurrant and strawberry number: “You can use up tomatoes in the paste, too.” Otherwise, if you have plums and damsons, take inspiration from Japanese umeboshi: “That has a high percentage of salt – I use 15% per 100g fruit. Layer the salt and plums in jars and, if it’s really dry, pour over water; otherwise, just crush a couple of the plums so their juices create a brine with the salt.” The brine can then be used like a plummy soy sauce, De Thample says: “Having a few jars stored away always makes me feel like I’m winning.” Damsons are also a dream in flavoured liquors, says Kenji Morimoto, regular Guardian contributor and author of Ferment: “That’s a really nice way to capture their flavour, and all you need is vodka, the fruit and rock [or granulated] sugar.Got a culinary dilemma? Email feast@theguardian.com Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Why did Modi urge Putin to end Ukraine war - and will he listen?
primary_source.content: Watch: Modi tells Putin "move on from an endless war to an end of war" "Every day spent in war pushes humanity back, and every step taken towards peace fills humanity with new hope and enthusiasm," Modi said on Monday. Modi, whose country's economy depends heavily on discounted oil from Moscow, has made several similar pleas to Putin since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. BBC correspondents in Delhi and Moscow look at what lies behind Modi's renewed appeal for peace, and Putin's response. Modi's comments on ending the war in Ukraine are not surprising and don't suggest any tactical change in India's foreign policy. In fact, speaking on the sidelines of a regional summit in 2022 - less than a year into the conflict - Modi told Putin publicly that "now is not the time for war".

primary_source.content: Bengaluru: Cricketer MS Dhoni has invested in AI-powered English-speaking and communication platform SpeakX. stories.primary_headline: Without new landers or rovers, it's helicopters or bust for NASA's Mars program

primary_source.headline: Without new landers or rovers, it's helicopters or bust for NASA's Mars program
primary_source.content:
For the first time in more than 30 years, NASA has no firm plans to send any new landers or rovers to Mars. Instead, the agency's near-term focus at the red planet is on aerial drones, a pioneering mode of exploration that didn't seem realistic until a few years ago.
The first real use of drones for science at Mars will come with the SkyFall mission, a fleet of three helicopters set for launch as soon as late 2028. SkyFall's helicopters will ride to the red planet with NASA's Space Reactor-1 "Freedom" mission, which has the primary objective of demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space.
The launch schedule is aggressive for SR-1 Freedom and SkyFall, projects that didn't even exist in NASA's portfolio six months ago. NASA's plan for the SR-1 Freedom mission, estimated to cost $2.1 billion, calls for repurposing the core module of the canceled Gateway lunar space station into a testbed for nuclear electric propulsion. SkyFall will build on NASA's success with the Ingenuity helicopter, an experimental vehicle that became the first rotorcraft to fly on another world in 2021.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: If space data centers feel far-fetched, why not interstellar travel?

primary_source.headline: If space data centers feel far-fetched, why not interstellar travel?
primary_source.content: If they do it, it will be the first human-built object explicitly aimed for another star, and the sixth to leave our solar system. The mission is intended to cost about $15 million, and to launch in 2029. The non-profit is soliciting vendors to build the vehicle, funding to pay them, and scientific and artistic payloads to send, ala the sensors and Golden Record onboard NASA’s Voyager space probe, the first human spacecraft to leave our solar system. Most plans for interstellar exploration stumble when dealing with the vast distances involved and the comparatively slow methods we have to cross them. Voyager, launched in 1977, is now about 26 billion km from Earth; Alpha Centauri, the nearest star to our solar system, is 41 trillion km away. “I also got excited and then disappointed!” Johnston said of Starshot. “That’s the reason we are doing the mission. We are hell-bent on actually launching something in three years. … the big difference with most other [interstellar] missions and the Fermi Explorer is that the others all try to do it in a human lifetime, which means billion-dollar propulsion R&D programs. We have very deliberately picked 80,000 years as the minimum viable mission.” The plan is to launch the spacecraft on a rocket rideshare, then use efficient but low-power electric propulsion to slingshot the vehicle into a series of orbits that will eventually leave it bound for Alpha Centauri. The spacecraft is intended to be active for about 12 years before entering a final coast phase toward the other solar system. “If a dinosaur bone can last 200 million years then a metal box can easily survive the radiation environment we expect for 50,000 years,” Johnston said. “We don’t plan on powering spacecraft up at the end of the 80,000 years. We hope that a future human civilization will intercept it.”

stories.primary_headline: The final minutes before floodwater crashed through Nepal-China border

primary_source.headline: The final minutes before floodwater crashed through Nepal-China border
primary_source.content: Video shows scale of flash flood hitting Nepal-Tibet border A dark wall appears from behind the buildings at Gyirong, on the Chinese side of the Nepal-Tibet border. At first, it looks almost like a black cloud. Then it gathers shape and speed: water, mud, boulders, ice and rock surging down the valley. The CCTV footage, whose timestamp reads 10:59:53, went viral. For many, it was the first visual evidence of the sheer scale of the destruction that was unfolding. What happened in the minutes that followed is still difficult to reconstruct. But fragments of video and satellite imagery show much of the border complex swept away, with buildings that once crowded the valley floor simply gone. Electronic immigration records from Nepal's Rasuwagadhi border post are filling some gaps, as well as insights from its only surviving staff member. Tika Ram Pokharel, who happened to be in Kathmandu sitting an exam on the day, tells the BBC the crossing was unusually busy when floodwater hit. A satellite image shows the area around the Nepal-China border before devastating floods swept away buildings and vehicles

primary_source.content: The famous pueblos blancos in southern Spain’s Sierra de Grazalema natural park teem with wildlife amid a limestone wonderland of peaks‘The wind is in from Africa / Last night I couldn’t sleep.” Joni Mitchell has ear-wormed her way into my head as my wife and I step out from Zahara de la Sierra into the mountains of Sierra de Grazalema natural park. The Africa bit probably comes from yesterday’s visit to Zahara’s castle museum. Here, high above the tiled terracotta mosaic of village rooftops, we learned how the recapture of this picturesque hill town was a turning point in the Reconquista – the military campaign of the 1400s that saw the Catholics retake southern Spain after seven centuries of Moorish control. As for sleep deprivation, I may just have overdone it on last night’s tapas.Either way, Africa feels present as we tramp through the countryside of Andalucía, if only in the wildlife. The painted lady butterflies drifting over the flower-spangled verges, the turtle doves purring from the olive groves and the booted eagle drifting overhead: all are summer visitors recently blown in from the great continent to our south. stories.primary_headline: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban

primary_source.headline: 'I've never been to Afghanistan': Six million deportees forced to start over under the Taliban
primary_source.content: Watch: BBC's Lyse Doucet reports on the biggest cross-border movement of people "It feels good to be in my own country," 35-year-old Nazia says, just minutes after she crosses from Pakistan, where she was born, into Afghanistan. The Torkham crossing, known as "Zero Point", is where one hard life ends and another begins. "But I've never been to Afghanistan before and many people here don't even have enough bread to eat," Nazia sighs as she heads, two of her children in tow, toward registration counters festooned with white and black Taliban flags. Nearly her entire family, eight sisters and their offspring, were deported to Afghanistan this year from Pakistan or Iran. They are part of the biggest cross-border movement of people anywhere in the world.

stories.primary_headline: ‘I’m not nervous, I’m ready’: Tschabalala Self on racist vandals and her bold striding woman for the Fourth Plinth

primary_source.headline: ‘I’m not nervous, I’m ready’: Tschabalala Self on racist vandals and her bold striding woman for the Fourth Plinth
primary_source.content: The last time she displayed a sculpture in public in Britain, someone covered it in white paint. But, undeterred, the acclaimed artist is a placing a black woman in Trafalgar SquareTschabalala Self is relentlessly positive and unstoppably optimistic. The US artist is waiting for the unveiling of Lady in Blue, her new sculpture for the fourth plinth in Trafalgar Square, London, a towering, colourful painted bronze of a black woman striding (positively, optimistically) into the future. Self seems resolutely hopeful about the work, which is pretty impressive considering what happened to her last public sculpture in the UK. “Yeah,” she says, speaking from her home in upstate New York. “I mean, that was a completely racist act.”In 2022, Self unveiled Seated at Coal Drops Yard in King’s Cross, London. Like Lady in Blue, it was a vast, brightly painted bronze depiction of a black woman, this time seated demurely on a chair. After being shown at Coal Drops Yard without incident, it was moved to the De La Warr Pavilion in Bexhill-on-Sea, where the reception wasn’t quite as warm. “Within the first week,” says Self, “it was spraypainted white, but only on the skin of the sculpture.” As vandalism goes, it doesn’t get much more pointed, or racist. “The first feeling I had was just pain that my sculpture had been harmed. That someone had enacted violence on an object I had imbued with love and affection.” Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Trump admin shelves Cyclospora research despite record-breaking outbreak

primary_source.headline: Trump admin shelves Cyclospora research despite record-breaking outbreak
primary_source.content:
The Trump administration is halting vital federal research on the foodborne parasite Cyclospora, despite the record-breaking, nationwide outbreak of the diarrheal pathogen, according to Politico.
Of the three research programs that represent nearly all of the Cyclospora work at the US Department of Agriculture, two have been defunded, and the third is about to lose every scientist working on it. The Trump administration is shuttering the USDA's Beltsville Agricultural Research Center near Washington, DC, and moving its work to a location in Iowa. That includes relocating the remaining Cyclospora research.
Although the research is still funded, insiders told Politico that not one of the scientists working on the project plans to relocate from Maryland to Iowa. Instead, they are either retiring, being reassigned to a different project, or leaving the USDA's research services.Read full article

It took three years, but Coyote vs. Acme is finally in theaters and delighting audiences of all ages with its irresistible blend of slapstick humor, pointed satire, and even a warm fuzzy here and there. We're happy to report that the film was worth the wait.
(Some spoilers below but no major reveals.)
The film is based on a well-known satirical piece by Ian Frazier (also titled “Coyote vs. Acme”) published in The New Yorker in 1990. Development of a film version didn’t start until 2018, but some pretty talented people worked on the script, including James Gunn. stories.primary_headline: ‘Let Data Reign’: Trump decries opposition to data centres in US

primary_source.headline: ‘Let Data Reign’: Trump decries opposition to data centres in US - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Trump said on Monday that China is happy with what he called the “anti-Data Center movement”, suggesting that growing disapproval of the centres in the US would divert businesses to the world’s second largest economy. “The only reason that communities throughout the USA should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” Trump wrote in a social media post. “If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign.” As more data centres open across the country, in part to power the growing use of artificial intelligence, the facilities have been met with scepticism – by both Republican and Democratic voters. Data centres consume an enormous amount of electricity, raising concerns about the effect on the power grid, including possible outages and increased utility bills. Beyond electricity, environmental activists are ringing the alarm over the enormous amounts of water needed to cool down servers at data centres at a time when parts of the country are experiencing droughts.

stories.primary_headline: El Niño is now stronger than at any point in the last 1,000 years, study finds

primary_source.headline: El Niño is now stronger than at any point in the last 1,000 years, study finds
primary_source.content:
Every few years, El Niño or its cool counterpart, La Niña, shifts rainfall across the tropics, dries out Australia, floods parts of Peru, and rearranges the weather on most of the planet. The two are the warm and cold swings of a single system, the El Niño–Southern Oscillation, or ENSO, and that system is the largest source of year-to-year climate variation on Earth. Its swings sit atop the steadily rising temperatures driven by global warming.
But we didn't know whether global warming was making it stronger. It’s possible that the added energy in the atmosphere and oceans was causing its swings to be more dramatic.
“We've been seeing some very strong El Niño events in the late 20th and early 21st century, and what we didn't know was how unusual those are,” said Julie Cole, an environmental scientist at the University of Michigan. Because models disagree with one another and the instrumental data are too short to separate a trend, Cole’s team reconstructed a thousand-year-long ocean surface temperature record by analyzing fossilized Galápagos corals.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Ultramarathon runners train for months, sometimes years. But what happens when they don’t finish a race?

primary_source.headline: Ultramarathon runners train for months, sometimes years. But what happens when they don’t finish a race?
primary_source.content: DNF stands for ‘did not finish’ – the acronym no ultrarunner wants assigned to their race result. For amateurs, DNFing is loaded with emotion – but attrition rates are extremely commonDrenched, freezing, utterly miserable and with a GI catastrophe ready to blow, my internal conflict of quit/don’t quit was in full force. I was at about kilometre 56 of my 100km ultramarathon. After a cascade of bad decisions and worse weather, totally wretched, I shuffled and sobbed my way through the dark to the next checkpoint. By the time I got there at 62km, the resignation of dropping out had settled in. Months and months of training had come to nothing.Inside the checkpoint, soaked runners and their besieged crew were crowded into what resembled a field hospital triage unit. In the chaotic throng I found my crew, slumped down on to a bench and said: I’m pulling out. Continue reading...

primary_source.content: O2 Arena, LondonThe polymath rapper’s stage show, which also features SWAT teams and a warship, is truly bravura stuff – but you can’t help feeling this is an artist at a creative crossroadsA$AP Rocky dangles precariously from a helicopter, while beneath him black-clad SWAT officers brawl with his white-masked followers. This isn’t some cliffhanger setpiece from the rapper/actor’s latest film – it’s just how shows on his Don’t Be Dumb tour open. It’s a big production: there are further prop helicopters, including a smaller one up in the rafters from which he also raps (a reference to his single Helicopter), while the stage recreates the top deck of a naval warship, for reasons that never become clear.The bizarre set underscores a sense of a man in career transition, unsure who he is any more. In the eight years since his last album, this survivor of homelessness and incarceration became a father, three times, with Rihanna; he’s pivoting towards movies – good ones – and co-chairs the Met Gala. His new record sought to redefine him as an artist, juggling more of his trademark pugilistic rap with ambitious stylistic experiments and unexpected collaborations (Damon Albarn! Danny Elfman!). stories.primary_headline: Pocket's AI made my game ideas real. Now Meta controls the results.

primary_source.headline: Pocket's AI made my game ideas real. Now Meta controls the results.
primary_source.content:
The relatively recent rise of AI-assisted coding tools and the whole concept of "vibe coding" have effectively upended entire software development workflows. While these tools have been available to novice coders willing to put in the work to set them up, those with little to no coding experience could still be a little put off by the CLIs, IDEs, and terminal-based tinkering needed to create a complex AI-coded project these days.
Meta's latest AI-based project launch wants to make that kind of vibe coding as instantly accessible as posting on social media. Pocket—which launched in the US last Friday, August 21, after Meta acquired the staff behind the now-defunct vibe-coding app Gizmo in March—is a mobile app that lets users create fully functional interactive "gizmos" just by typing prompts into a text box, without even the option to look at a line of code. Those gizmos can then be shared with the world in a TikTok-style endless scroll complete with likes, comments, reposts, and all the other hallmarks of social media addiction.
After playing around with Pocket for the better part of a week, I found myself getting hooked on the simple process of quickly standing up functional, relatively feature-rich game prototypes simply by chatting with an LLM. But the result of all that time and AI effort is a couple of interactive toys that are effectively trapped in Meta's new walled garden, without any real way to turn them into something separate.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Xi, Modi and Putin attend SCO summit: What’s on the agenda?

primary_source.headline: Xi, Modi and Putin attend SCO summit: What’s on the agenda? - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Chinese President Xi Jinping, his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi have arrived in Kyrgyzstan’s capital Bishkek for the annual Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian is also attending the summit, which marks 25 years of its existence. The two-day summit, which kicked off on Monday, comes at a time when the world is grappling with the aftermath of the US-Israel war on Iran, which has upended global energy and financial markets, and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. This year’s summit is taking place in Bishkek under the motto: Together for Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity. Xi, Putin and Modi will be joined by the Iranian president and leaders of Pakistan, Uzbekistan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, among others. Xi has met Putin on the sidelines of the Summit. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn are also expected to attend the summit.

stories.primary_headline: A 12TB Steam “teraleak” spills more than a decade of lost PC gaming history

primary_source.headline: A 12TB Steam “teraleak” spills more than a decade of lost PC gaming history
primary_source.content:
Here at Ars, we're intimately familiar with data leaks surrounding Valve's games, hardware, and the workings of Steam itself. But nothing could have prepared us for this weekend's "terarelease" encompassing more than 12TB of content related to seemingly every title available on Steam between 2003 and 2013.
What's being sold as an "as-complete-as-possible ... content server dump" of Steam's defunct "Steam2" server architecture from that time period is now circulating around via a BitTorrent tracker that Valve seems unlikely to ever completely purge from the Internet. The massive collection includes thousands of "depots" representing what seems to be every version of every game uploaded to those old Steam2 servers. That includes public release builds, of course, but in many cases also covers previously unseen pre-release, prototype, and playtest versions of popular titles published by Valve and third-party Steam publishers.
Steam2: Electric Boogaloo
The reason this weekend's leaked content cuts off abruptly in 2013 is because that's when Valve updated its content distribution system from "Steam2" to the current SteamPipe system. In moving from a proprietary file distribution format to standard HTTP file trees, the new system removed various update approval bottlenecks on Valve's end and streamlined update and patch downloads so they only reflected file differentials.Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Educated? Skilled? Ambitious? Traffickers are looking for you

primary_source.headline: Educated? Skilled? Ambitious? Traffickers are looking for you - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Good salary. Visa sponsored. Flight included. Applicants must be educated, fluent in English and confident online. It sounds like a great opportunity for a young graduate, but it is the bait in a trafficking operation. The advertised job does not exist. On arrival, the person’s passport is taken. They are moved to a compound they cannot leave and are forced to run online scams: impersonating strangers, building false relationships and persuading people thousands of kilometres away to send money. Those who miss their targets may be beaten, starved or placed in solitary confinement. Their families may sell land or take on debt to raise money to pay for their release. I heard versions of this story firsthand during a recent visit to Rwanda, where I met two survivors who had been trafficked through fraudulent job offers. They were fluent in English and comfortable with technology. They had been looking for the same thing as millions of other young people: a good job and the chance to build a better future. Those qualities made them valuable to the traffickers. They were given scripts and forced to impersonate women online, build romantic relationships with people in Europe and persuade them to send money.

stories.primary_headline: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers

primary_source.headline: Inside Meta’s push to put robots to work in data centers
primary_source.content:
Meta is testing robots that can plug in cables, reset servers, and handle other tasks inside its data centers, according to several current and former workers familiar with the projects. The ongoing effort, which has not been previously reported, may eventually allow Meta to operate its rapidly expanding data center footprint with fewer humans, keeping labor costs in check as its spending on AI infrastructure soars.
Meta is using robots and related hardware from several different vendors, including Watney Robotics, Kinova, and ABB, according to the same workers, who asked to remain anonymous because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Kinova and ABB declined to comment. Watney didn’t respond to requests for comment.
In one experiment, Meta is evaluating whether a Kinova Gen3 robotic arm could be used for power cycling or cutting off electricity to servers. The company is also testing a different robot to swap networking cables. One Meta data center worker estimates that if it’s successful, the bot could replace up to 80 percent of some people’s workloads. “We thought those of us performing the physical tasks were safe for a while, but not anymore,” says the worker. “It’s coming for us all, unfortunately.”Read full article

stories.primary_headline: Toxic waste of war on Gaza reached Israel

primary_source.headline: Toxic waste of war on Gaza reached Israel - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Earlier this month, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and representatives of the Board of Peace agreed to set up a working group on sanitation and public health affecting both Israel and Gaza. Its membership and detailed operating structure are yet to be made public. It appears it has finally dawned on the Israeli authorities that the consequences of the unrelenting ecocidal destruction of Gaza were eventually going to hit Israel. The toxic leftovers of war – untreated sewage and contaminated rubble – are now a problem for Israeli public health as well. Gaza shares the Mediterranean, coastal ecosystems and coastal aquifers with Israel. The destruction of its electric power and sanitation infrastructure forces over 100,000 cubic metres of raw, untreated sewage into the Mediterranean Sea or on land every day. Because in this part of the Mediterranean currents move primarily from south to north, this waste is carried straight up the coast into Israeli waters. The Ashkelon desalination plant in southern Israel has been forced to shut down multiple times due to high faecal bacteria contamination from Gaza’s wastewater. Raw sewage also triggers toxic algae blooms blocking and damaging desalination filtration systems, as well as creating dead zones where fishing would normally happen. Wastewater toxins, heavy metals and pathogens are absorbed by local marine life. Because fish migrate across maritime boundaries, contaminated seafood poses a direct health hazard to Palestinian as well as Israeli consumers. Raw sewage carries the same pathogens afflicting Gaza into the shared marine environment. Its northward drift directly impacts Israeli coastal cities. Although pathogens can persist and migrate under certain conditions, pathogen contaminated groundwater is unlikely to feed into Israeli municipal water supplies, but can still affect the shared aquifer and surrounding environment.

primary_source.headline: US says far-right provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos has been deported to UK - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: On Saturday, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed Yiannopoulos’s removal a day earlier. “He chose to overstay his welcome in violation of our nation’s laws,” the department posted on social media, in announcing Yiannopoulos’s arrest. He entered the country through New York City in May 2019. After Yiannopoulos missed an immigration hearing earlier this year, a judge issued a final order for his removal on July 22. In announcing Yiannopoulos’s detention on Friday, the DHS encouraged noncitizens who overstayed their visas to self-deport. “We encourage every person here illegally to take advantage of this offer and reserve the chance to come back to the U.S. the right legal way to live the American dream,” the department wrote. “If not, you will be arrested and deported without a chance to return.” Yiannopoulos has not publicly weighed in on his deportation, with his usually active social media account on X staying silent since his detention.

stories.primary_headline: Keir Starmer announces he is standing down as MP

primary_source.headline: Keir Starmer announces he is standing down as MP
primary_source.content: Since he resigned as prime minister in July, there was speculation over whether Sir Keir would stay on as MP The move will trigger a by-election in the London seat of Holborn and St Pancras, long a Labour stronghold, which he has represented since 2015. Sir Keir, who left Downing Street in July, had previously said he would stay on as an MP until the next UK general election, which is not due until 2029. But in a surprise statement hours before his successor Andy Burnham made his debut in the House of Commons, he said he was resigning to work on issues such as international affairs and violence against women and girls. "He has given this country a lifetime of public service, particularly for those fighting for justice," he added. "His leadership took our party from one of its worst defeats to its best victories and created a platform to change this country for the better. We will use it well, and we wish his family the very best for the future."

stories.primary_headline: This startup is fuel-injecting hydrogen to make cargo ships more efficient

primary_source.headline: This startup is fuel-injecting hydrogen to make cargo ships more efficient
primary_source.content: It’s one of the most iconic scenes in the Fast & Furious film franchise: Paul Walker’s thumb comes off the steering wheel and smashes a small red button, pumping nitrous oxide into the engine of his Mitsubishi Eclipse and giving the car an explosive boost. “Instead of getting power, we actually say to the engine: ‘Hey, reduce the fuel [flow] to the engine, we don’t need as much because we have some nitrous. It’s [just] called hydrogen,’” he told TechCrunch in an exclusive interview. The small team based in the San Francisco Bay Area has developed this hydrogen injection system as a retrofit, which it claims can be installed in less than two weeks without needing a dry dock. It cuts fuel use and emissions by more than 20%, and can save some vessels as much as $500,000 in annual costs, according to the startup. Newlight does this by constantly monitoring the diesel engine and finding optimal moments, down to the millisecond level, to inject the hydrogen fuel. That includes measuring exhaust temperature, combustion pressure, and air intake pressure, and increasing or decreasing the hydrogen flow every time a piston moves inside the engine’s cylinders. The startup says this hybrid system has completed its first long-range commercial voyage: an 8,500-nautical mile trip from Singapore to Ghana. Newlight installed its tech on a 650-foot-long Lomar Shipping bulk carrier ship for the test. The startup said its system reduced fuel consumption by 24% and carbon dioxide emissions by 28%. “It was amazing,” Haran Cohen Hillel, Cohen’s co-founder and the CEO of Newlight, said of the month-long voyage. “Being onboard and seeing the system operate in real conditions was a completely different experience from anything we had done in the lab.”

stories.primary_headline: 100 low-performing agricultural districts show marked progress under PM-DDKY: Centre

primary_source.headline: 100 low-performing agricultural districts show marked progress under PM-DDKY: Centre
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The government on Tuesday said 100 low-performing agricultural districts have registered clear improvement across key parameters, including crop yield and access to credit, since the rollout of the Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana (PM-DDKY).Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan reviewed the scheme’s progress.&nbsp;Shivraj Singh Chouhan releases Rs 21.35 crore scholarships for over 6,000 agriculture students via DBTApproved by the Union Cabinet in July 2025 and launched in October 2025, PM-DDKY is being implemented through the convergence of 36 central schemes of 11 ministries, along with state schemes and private-sector participation. It targets 100 districts selected on the basis of low yields, cropping intensity and agricultural credit.The average score of these districts across the six scheme objectives rose from 22.54 in April 2026 to 38.85 in July 2026, an increase of 16.31 points, an official statement said. Progress is tracked monthly via the PM-DDKY dashboard using 121 indicators (74 output and 47 outcome) drawn from the converging schemes.Scores improved in every objective: agricultural productivity from 2.53 to 6.70; crop diversification and sustainable practices from 5.60 to 8.65; post-harvest storage capacity from 2.61 to 3.82; irrigation infrastructure from 1.65 to 4.20; access to agricultural credit from 2.81 to 5.59; and governance and service delivery from 7.94 to 10.33, the statement said.&nbsp;Between January and July 2026, 6,90,530 farmers and 88,961 extension workers received skill training, while an additional 2,20,683 were trained in natural farming. The ministry stressed the need to strengthen monitoring so that the focus shifts from activities and expenditure to measurable outcomes and actual benefits reaching farmers.

stories.primary_headline: National Conference, BJP set for rival protests in J&K on Wednesday

primary_source.headline: National Conference, BJP set for rival protests in J&K on Wednesday
primary_source.content: Srinagar: The National Conference (NC) will gherao BJP offices in Srinagar and Jammu on Wednesday (September 2) over statehood and other demands, while the Civil Secretariat will protest outside the Civil Secretariat in Srinagar over the Omar Abdullah government’s performance.The rival protests come amid an intensifying political contest, with the NC seeking action from the Centre on restoration of statehood, constitutional safeguards and the reservation issue.J&K: Aga Ruhullah to resign as MP, quit National Conference on November 3 amid Article 370 riftOn the other hand, BJP has accused the NC government of failing to address electricity tariffs, unemployment, recruitment and delays in local-body elections.The NC said its mobilisation was aimed at pressing the Union government to act on assurances concerning Jammu and Kashmir made before Parliament and the Supreme Court.“The mandate of the people of Jammu & Kashmir is not a blank cheque. It must be respected, not taken for granted,” the party said.The proposed protests follow the NC’s July 20 statehood mobilisation in Delhi, where police stopped party leaders from reaching Jantar Mantar.The party subsequently held a demonstration in the vicinity of Constitution Club, with Omar Abdullah and Farooq Abdullah among those who participated.Statehood remains the NC government’s principal demand from the Centre. It has also sought changes to the reservation structure and clearance of the related file.The BJP’s planned Secretariat gherao, meanwhile, is directed at the elected government and focuses on issues including the recent electricity tariff increase, unemployment, recruitment and delays in holding panchayat and urban local-body elections.The competing protests will bring the NC-Centre and NC-BJP political contests onto the streets on the same day, underscoring the widening political divide in the Union Territory.The NC said its demonstrations would remain peaceful and democratic.

stories.primary_headline: 'Stand By Me' bags and dresses: Kerala nuns fight for survival amid legal battle

primary_source.headline: 'Stand By Me' bags and dresses: Kerala nuns fight for survival amid legal battle
primary_source.content: Thiruvananthapuram: Three nuns in Kerala, who are on a legal fight against former Jalandhar bishop Franco Mulakkal over sexual assault allegations, are bringing out products like bags and dresses for ladies for their survival as their congregation had stopped support to them.The sisters at the St Francis Mission Home at Kuravilangad in Kottayam, are bringing out the products under the brand 'Stand By Me- Survivors of gender-based violence'.'Women appearing at public platforms will lead to great destruction, should stay at home': Kerala cleric sparks rowThey are now participating in exhibitions cum sales, the latest one to be held at Kozhikode on September 5.After they initiated the legal fight against Mulakkal, they were facing severe neglect from the congregation. The congregation eventually stopped providing financial and other support to them. A few other nuns who stood with them were also forced to leave the convent."We were left with no option for survival. Hence we initiated making bags and dress items for ladies. Initially we used to sell through our personal contacts. Later some groups like the Women Entrepreneur Network started supporting us. We already took part in exhibition cum sales in Bengaluru and Thiruvananthapuram and got good response," Sister Ranit told DH.A 20-minute stop that saved 31 lives: Kerala group returns from flood-hit NepalSisters Alphy and Ancitta are the others involved in the struggle for survival.Even as Mulakkal was acquitted by a trial court, an appeal is pending before the Kerala High Court. The nuns are determined to fight the case until he is punished.Mulakkal was accused of sexually assaulting a nun several times between 2014 and 2016 at the convent. The Kottayam additional sessions court acquitted Mulakkal in the case.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Not just Hollywood crap’: Mike Leigh on the East End communist who brought world cinema to the UK

primary_source.headline: ‘Not just Hollywood crap’: Mike Leigh on the East End communist who brought world cinema to the UK
primary_source.content: A new season at the BFI celebrates Contemporary Films and its founder Charles Cooper, who bet on Britain taking to Ingmar Bergman, Yasujiro Ozu, Stayajjit Ray – and a young Mike LeighOccasionally, vital pieces of the cultural jigsaw disappear without anyone really noticing. This, sadly, was the fate of Contemporary Films, the British film distributor that popularised sophisticated, grownup international cinema – foreign language mostly – in the UK, and heralded the arrival of the auteur generation with directors such as Ingmar Bergman, Satyajit Ray, Andrzej Wajda and Yasujiro Ozu.Contemporary, and its founder Charles Cooper, weren’t the only game in town – Kenneth Rive’s Gala was a fellow traveller – but Contemporary got there first, setting up shop in 1951, first with short films for the then popular film society sector, and moving into features with the 1952 Japanese film Children of Hiroshima. Its marketplace clout faded rapidly in the early 1990s, when it was a victim of changing industry practices. But amazingly, the company is still with us – and is planning a 75th anniversary series of screenings to showcase its history. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: India's manufacturing output growth slips to 5-year low on weak demands

primary_source.headline: India's manufacturing output growth slips to 5-year low on weak demands
primary_source.content: New Delhi: India’s manufacturing output dipped to a five-year low in August, dragged by weak demands indicating caution amid weak monsoon and global uncertainties, as per an industry survey report released by&nbsp;S&P Global on Tuesday.&nbsp;Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) for manufacturing slipped to 52.8 in August from 53.5 in the previous month.India’s manufacturing PMI slips to 5-year low on weak demandsThe manufacturing PMI in August was the lowest in five years. It was also below its long-run average of 54.2. A PMI reading above 50.0 signals an expansion in the sector, whereas a value below 50.0 indicates contraction.This is the third consecutive month of decline in manufacturing PMI. The August figure “signalled a loss of momentum as growth of both output and new orders slowed to five-year lows,” S&P Global said in its monthly report, which is based on a survey conducted among around 400 manufacturers.“Firms reported softer demand conditions, which subsequently led to weaker increases in buying levels and stocks, as well as a mild decline in employment,” it said.Demand trends softened across two of the three industrial groups tracked by the survey, with consumer goods the exception. The surveyed firms attributed the weaker upturn to challenging market conditions and subdued appetite for some products.Production volumes in August increased at its weakest pace in five years. Firms linked the slowdown to softer demand conditions and more limited increases in new order volumes.“The output index fell to its lowest level since August 2021, signalling that production is still expanding but at a markedly slower pace,” said Pranjul Bhandari, Chief India Economist at HSBC.“Employment edged into a mild contraction in August, the first decline after more than two years of job growth. Meanwhile, input cost pressures continued to ease, and manufacturers responded by raising selling prices more modestly,” Bhandari added.The softer sales environment was reflected in workforce and purchasing decisions. Manufacturing employment fell&nbsp;for the first time in two-and-a-half years, though the rate of decline was only fractional.Companies that reduced staffing levels mainly cited lower business requirements. Input buying still expanded for the sixty-second successive month, but did so at the weakest rate over this period as some firms restocked while others trimmed purchases in line with softer demand, S&P Global noted in the report.Manufacturers continued to face higher costs for materials, including steel, and transport, but the overall rate of inflation in August was the lowest in six months. Softer cost pressures helped firms limit increases in their selling prices. The rate of output charge inflation was the slowest in 45 months and below its long-run trend.Business confidence remained subdued.&nbsp;Around 16% of survey participants forecast higher output over the coming 12 months, while the remainder expect no change from present levels.

stories.primary_headline: Karnataka-Maharashtra border dispute: Government asks Belagavi City Corporation to follow 1988 resolution of legislature

primary_source.headline: Karnataka-Maharashtra border dispute: Government asks Belagavi City Corporation to follow 1988 resolution of legislature
primary_source.content: Belagavi: The Karnataka government has directed Belagavi City Corporation (BCC) to pass pro-state resolution as passed in the legislature on March 23, 1988 which states that implementation of Mahajan Commission report for resolving the Karnataka-Maharashtra boundary dispute was unavoidable.Kannada organisations for the past five months have undertaken a movement demanding that BCC pass pro-state resolution stating that Belagavi is inseparable part of the state. They had also submitted representations stating their demands to Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, Urban Development Minister Dr Yatindra Siddaramaiah along with holding talks in this regard with Public Works Department and District In-charge Minister Satish Jarkiholi.Many express disappointment over Belagavi Police Commissioner Bhushan Borase’s transferBelagavi District Kannada Organisations Action Committee President Ashok Chandargi told reporters here on Tuesday that we have won first battle in our movement demanding that the civic body pass pro-state resolution.We had first made the demand in the month of March, however the issue was not discussed in the council meetings held in the month of March and April. In the council meeting held in May, Mayor Preeti Kamkar had passed resolution seeking guidelines from government as Maharashtra has filed suit in the Supreme Court regarding Karnataka-Maharashtra boundary dispute.He said, government after considering all aspects and demands has sent copy of the resolution passed by the legislature during the tenure of then chief minister Ramakrishna Hegde which was tabled by H K Patil.Resolution reads, “Implementation of Mahajan Commission report is necessary regarding the Karnataka-Maharashtra boundary dispute. Delay in implementation of the report has been leading Maharashtra leaders using it to their advantage and creating friction between both the states. Implementing recommendations of Mahajan Commission report were binding on both the states and we urge the centre to implement it.” BCC if does not pass the resolution, we shall urge the government to supercede it for not honouring guidelines of the government, he said.Government has also cautioned commissioner against sending such issues to it. Commissioner had to be reprimanded due to the mistake of mayor, he said.

stories.primary_headline: ‘False and objectionable’: UP Cong president Ajay Rai files defamation case against CM Yogi over ‘fish feast’ remarks

primary_source.headline: ‘False and objectionable’: UP Cong president Ajay Rai files defamation case against CM Yogi over ‘fish feast’ remarks
primary_source.content: Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai on Tuesday filed a defamation case against chief minister Yogi Adityanath over the latter’s reported remarks regarding organizing a ‘fish feast’ by the former in Ayodhya recently.Rai filed the defamation case in the Civil Court here.In his petition, Rai said that the allegations leveled in this connection by Adityanath were ‘false’ and ‘objectionable’.'An insult to Hindu traditions': UP CM Adityanath hits Congress over fish feast during Shravana‘’An attempt was made to tarnish my public image and reputation by presenting incorrect facts…….leveling wrong and baseless allegations against anyone in public life is a serious matter,’’ he said in his petition.It was alleged that a ‘fish feast’ was organised during Rai’s event in Ayodhya in the ongoing sacred Hindu month of Shravana. Several Ayodhya based seers and Adityanath had termed it as reflective of Congress’ ‘anti-Sanatan’ mindset and sought an apology from the grand old party.‘’Organising a fish feast during Shravana is an insult to Sanatan Dharma as well as Ayodhya and Congress must tender a public apology,’’ Mahant Bharat, an Ayodhya based seer had said.He said that Congress had no ‘respect’ for the Hindu sentiments and ‘Sanatan Dharma’ and that such an insult would never be tolerated by the seers.Adityanath had also, while addressing a public meeting, slammed Congress saying that it was an ‘insult’ to Hindu traditions and religious beliefs. ‘’Congress has always been anti-Sanatan’’, he had remarked.A bone of contention: BJP picks on Congress over fish feast in Ayodhya during 'Sawan' monthRai, however, denied the allegations stating that he had attended a program organised by the ‘Nishad’ (fishermen) community in Ayodhya but no non-vegetarian food was served there. ‘’BJP is insulting the Nishad community by levelling such allegations,’’ he added.He had also challenged the BJP to furnish proof of their allegations.The controversy had erupted after a video, purportedly showing fish being served at the event attended by Rai, went viral on social media platforms.

stories.primary_headline: Led by Rahul Gandhi, Maharashtra Opposition mounts vote-chori charge

primary_source.headline: Led by Rahul Gandhi, Maharashtra Opposition mounts vote-chori charge
primary_source.content: Mumbai: With more than 2.06 crore electors excluded from Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll after the SIR exercise, the Maha Vikas Aghadi-INDIA opposition reiterated allegations of vote-chori with Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi spearheading the charge.&nbsp;It may be mentioned that after the 2024 Maharashtra Legislative Assembly elections, in which the BJP-led Maha Yuti swept the polls with a never-seen-before verdict, Gandhi had made allegations of vote theft.&nbsp;“The BJP and the 'Vote Theft Commission' keep changing their tactics, and they will continue to do so—the goal remains just one: BJP's victory at any cost, and the end of India's democracy,” Gandhi said slamming the BJP and the Election Commission.&nbsp;'Only goal is BJP's victory at any cost' | Rahul Gandhi revives ‘vote chori’ campaign“In Maharashtra&nbsp;&nbsp;in 2024, suddenly, 39 lakh new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft.&nbsp;Before the SIR, Maharashtra had 9.78 crore voters, of whom 78.86 per cent made it to the draft roll.”The Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee (MPCC) pointed out that the&nbsp;list&nbsp;also includes&nbsp;the&nbsp;names of suspicious&nbsp;and&nbsp;unmapped&nbsp;voters;&nbsp;but no mark has been put on those names. “This will create confusion among the voters, these voters will be called for a hearing by giving a notice,” it said, demanding that&nbsp;a booth-wise list of voters to whom notices are&nbsp;to be issued&nbsp;be published immediately and made available to political parties.Congress has expressed fear that&nbsp;BLOs will use the same method&nbsp;as in Maharashtra where 1.52 crore voters were not found or were shown as permanently displaced&nbsp;,&nbsp;and that crores more voters will be excluded from the voter list.Congress MLA Amin Patel said&nbsp;that in the new list, the names of approximately two crore people have been deleted from Maharashtra, while around 35–40 percent of names have been deleted in Mumbai.“When the SIR process began, we had written to the Election Commission and raised the issue, telling them that the process was not being carried out properly. BLOs were not going to people’s homes, and people were being marked as unavailable,” Patel said, alleging that the SIR process was rigged.&nbsp;NCP national spokesperson and secretary Clyde Crasto said: “Shocking that two crore voters’ names deleted from the draft Maharashtra SIR list. Some of these voters voted for the BJP in the last elections. So does this deletion of names now give any validity to the BJP led government in Maharashtra?”Congress leader in the Legislative Council Satej Patil said that Gandhi has flagged the sudden addition of around 39 lakh voters in just 5 months between 2024 Lok Sabha and&nbsp;Vidhan Sabha polls. “Those were more than the previous 5 years' addition and now comes a sharp drop,” he said, demanding that the EC must provide&nbsp;&nbsp;full comparable machine-readable data of 2024 Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha and pre-SIR rolls.BJP defends processBJP MLA and spokesperson Ram Kadam said that the BLOs have visited the homes. "The SIR process is a transparent process. Anyone can sit at home and get their name registered, and the BLOs are going door to door,” he said and wanted to know what exactly the opposition wants. “There are names appearing four times in the voter list, and there are also names of people who have died. Should those names not be removed? What is the opposition's strategy behind keeping the same names four times?,” he said and alleged that the Congress created a fake narrative ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls that the Constitution is going to be changed.&nbsp;

stories.primary_headline: 'Only goal is BJP's victory at any cost' | Rahul Gandhi revives ‘vote chori’ campaign

primary_source.headline: 'Only goal is BJP's victory at any cost' | Rahul Gandhi revives ‘vote chori’ campaign
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: Citing the deletion of 2.07 crore names from Maharashtra draft electoral rolls, top Congress leader Rahul Gandhi revived the ‘vote chori’ campaign on Tuesday claiming that the “goal of the BJP and ‘Vote Chori’ Commission” is to ensure the saffron party's victory.He also recalled his claim of suspicious addition of nearly 40 lakh voters in five months between Lok Sabha and Assembly elections in Maharashtra and said for a government built on 'vote chori', the people are not important and that is why the BJP neither listens to the people nor obeys their command."The BJP and the 'Vote Theft Commission' keep changing their tactics, and they will continue to do so -- the goal remains just one: BJP's victory at any cost, and the end of India's democracy," he said on 'X'.भाजपा और 'वोट चोरी आयोग' के तरीके बदलते रहते हैं, और बदलते रहेंगे - मकसद बस एक ही है: किसी भी क़ीमत पर BJP की जीत, और भारत के लोकतंत्र का अंत।महाराष्ट्र 2024 - लोकसभा और विधानसभा चुनाव के बीच अचानक 39 लाख नए वोटर जुड़ गए। मैंने तब भी कहा था, आज भी कहता हूँ: यह वोट चोरी थी।…&mdash; Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) September 1, 2026
 

His remarks came as Maharashtra Chief Electoral Office released the draft electoral rolls on Monday following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in which 2,06,88,487 names were deleted from the voter list, which had 9,78,54,049 names. The draft list has 7,71,65,562 names, which is 78.86% of the pre-SIR voter list."Maharashtra 2024 -- suddenly, 39 lakh new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Assembly elections. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft. Bengal 2026 -- of the names struck off in the SIR, 91% had to be reinstated after appeals. That means 9 out of every 10 names were wrongly deleted, and added back only after the election. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft," Rahul said.Over 3,400 SIR forms found at private photocopy centre in Maharashtra; 5 BLOs suspended"And now in Maharashtra, 2.07 crore voters have been removed from the draft lis -- that's every fifth voter. Lok Sabha 2024: 9.29 crore. Assembly 2024: 9.7 crore. SIR 2026 (draft list): 7.78 crore. Which list was correct? For a government built on vote theft, the people are not important -- that's why this BJP neither listens to the people nor obeys their command," he said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the BJP's “conspiracy to hollow out Indian democracy by stealing votes” is coming out into the open.&nbsp;“Where it suits the BJP, voters are added. Where it doesn't, votes are split to perpetrate 'vote theft'. Instead of acting as the guardian of fair elections, the EC is functioning like the 'Save BJP's Chair Commission'...The country is now uniting against vote theft. The nation has understood the BJP's conspiracy. The thief has been caught. Punishment will surely be meted out for holding democracy captive.”Congress Media and Publicity Department Chairman Pawan Khera said either the electoral rolls for the 2024 Maharashtra Assembly election were flawless, in which case the SIR has led to wrongful deletions or those rolls were questionable in which case Devendra Fadnavis is heading an "illegitimate" government."Only one of these two scenarios can be true. But either way, one conclusion is inescapable: The integrity of India’s elections has been compromised. And Gyanesh Gupta is the culprit," he said quoting Rahul's post. Khera has referred to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as Gyanesh Gupta.

stories.primary_headline: ‘Get up, get breakfast, noise’: the teen going viral for enduring all 400 of Merzbow’s ear-splitting albums

primary_source.headline: ‘Get up, get breakfast, noise’: the teen going viral for enduring all 400 of Merzbow’s ear-splitting albums
primary_source.content: The infamous Japanese noise artist has a vast and forbidding catalogue that commands a cult fandom. Sam Andrews, 18, is vlogging his way through the lot – and taking a stand for deep listeningAn Instagram Reel that looks like an 80s coming-of-age movie pops up on your feed. It’s four teenage boys in an American-style basement – comfy sofas, guitars, ping pong table – jeering and laughing. But they aren’t secretly drinking beer or planning on sneaking out. They’re brandishing a vinyl copy of Pulse Demon, the most popular album from the cult Japanese noise artist Merzbow, and subjecting themselves to its brutally harsh sound in full, for fun. “I think this is the Book of Revelation: The Soundtrack,” one guy blurts out, a vague look of fear in his eyes.Merzbow, real name Masami Akita, is the world’s most renowned noise artist. Since 1979, Akita has released more than 400 recordings, which range from a 10-hour long album misleadingly titled Merzbient (it’s anything but ambient) to a free-noise supergroup called Flying Testicle. Since February, Sam Andrews, the video’s 18-year-old creator, has been attempting to listen to every one, and is documenting his progress online each day. “I think of my day in album-size chunks,” he says, laughing. “It’s like, get up at seven, get breakfast and then headphones in: noise.” Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Another head rolls in Pakistan cricket as selector Misbah resigns after shock sacking of coach Sarfaraz

primary_source.headline: Another head rolls in Pakistan cricket as selector Misbah resigns after shock sacking of coach Sarfaraz
primary_source.content: Pakistan cricket plunged into further turmoil after selector and ex-captain Misbah-ul-Haq resigned following the shock sacking of red-ball head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed in the wake of successive Test defeats to England in the ongoing three-match Test series. It may be recalled that the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) sacked Ahmed and replaced him with current white-ball coach Mike Hesson for the last Test in Birmingham.Lord's Test | Robinson the star as England thrash Pakistan to clinch seriesPCB also sent seven players home from the England tour and replaced bowling coach Umar Gul with Australian Ashley Noffke in a move that has drawn widespread criticism in Pakistan.The shake-up follows Pakistan's embarrassing innings and 103-run defeat at Headingley and a 194-run drubbing at Lord's, giving England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Seven players -- Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad -- were sent home, with five of them replaced by uncapped players.Former Pakistan captain and selection committee member Misbah later resigned in protest at not being consulted over the changes, as reported by AFP news agency."Misbah sent his resignation to the PCB by email and is yet to receive a reply," sources close to Misbah said.Several former coaches and players were left shocked over the unprecedented shake-up with a match still to play."What an absolutely ridiculous situation," said ex-Pakistan coach Mickey Arthur.Former selector and Pakistan spinner Tauseef Ahmed called the changes "unprecedented and unjust", adding they had "created a polluted atmosphere in Pakistan cricket."You don't treat your senior players like this," said Tauseef.After having lost the first two Tests and the series, Pakistan have nothing to play for, but pride in the third match that starts on September 9.(With inputs from agencies)

stories.primary_headline: Four states move Supreme Court seeking quashing of 116 FIRs over NEET protests

primary_source.headline: Four states move Supreme Court seeking quashing of 116 FIRs over NEET protests
primary_source.content: New Delhi: States of Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Assam on Tuesday approached the Supreme Court seeking the quashing of 116 FIRs registered in connection with student protests held in July over the alleged NEET exam paper leak.They cited the central government’s commitment to the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on July 25 that the cases would be withdrawn if the agitations were called off.The states urged the court to invoke its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution.&nbsp;SC quashes FIRs on NEET protesters, allows fresh cases against 2,873 personsThe applications came a day after the Centre filed a similar plea to quash Delhi Police FIRs against protesters while seeking permission to register a single FIR against 2,873 persons with grave criminal antecedents.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta on Tuesday urged a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to list the states’ applications along with the Centre’s plea.&nbsp;The moves precede the CJP’s announcement of a fresh protest in Delhi on September 5, with the party contending that the Centre had not honoured its commitment.Bihar sought the quashing of 69 FIRs registered between July 20 and 27 across several districts, including cases at Gandhi Maidan and Kotwali in Patna, Gopalganj Town, Siwan Town, Jehanabad, Katihar Town, Muzaffarpur Town, Bihar Sharif, Bhagwan Bazar, Dumra, Punora, Lalganj and Bettiah.Maharashtra placed 34 FIRs before the court, covering cases in Nagpur, Mumbai, Pune, Jalgaon, Buldhana, Amravati and other locations. These included multiple FIRs from Shivaji Park and Sitabuldi police stations, as well as Ganesh Peth, Sadar, Azad Maidan, Chembur, Wadi, Deccan, Ambi and Ramtek. The state said that pursuant to the Centre’s July 25 decision, it no longer wished to pursue or investigate the listed cases.West Bengal also sought relief in respect of eight FIRs — one at Entally police station and seven at Hare Street police station. The state has undertaken not to oppose similar relief for any other related FIR that may come to its notice and has assured that no fresh FIR will be filed for the covered incidents.Assam listed five FIRs for quashing, stating that it no longer wished to pursue or investigate them following the central government’s July 25 decision.

Here are 5 such Matrimonial sites in India that Punjabi families tend to use.1. Royal MatrimonialStarted in 2006, Royal Matrimonial has spent close to two decades working specifically within the Punjabi community. That focus shows in how they operate. Instead of just handing users a list of profiles and leaving them to figure things out, the team sits with families, understands what they actually want, and narrows down suggestions accordingly. Registration doesn't cost anything, and members also get invited to online Swayamvaras where they can interact directly. There are three packages to pick from, Basic, Vicholia and Elite Vicholia, depending on how much hand-holding a family wants. Most reviews point to the same thing, the coordinators actually follow up instead of going silent after registration.2. Bharat MatrimonyBharat Matrimony has been in existence since 1997 and has become one of the leading players in the field. The company even made it to the Limca Book of Records for conducting the maximum number of marriages through its website, an indication of the huge user base. Registration on the site is free, and therefore you can browse for some time and then decide whether to subscribe to the paid membership service or not. Members can then decide if they wish to invest in one of the many packages available such as Gold, Platinum, Diamond and Assisted Matrimony. With a presence that covers multiple communities, including Punjabi and Sikh, this site is a popular choice for its sheer reach.3. Shaadi.comShaadi.com is another veteran in the field, having been in existence since 1996 and boasting over 18 million registered members. Shaadi Live, the company's latest offering, facilitates quick one-on-one conversations with up to 10 matches in a single hour, with each conversation lasting no longer than 5 minutes.Registration is free, and so is basic browsing, applying for matches and chatting with them. The Gold, Diamond and Platinum packages come into play when it comes to exchanging phone numbers and attending meet-ups/Shaadi events.4. JeevansathiJeevansathi entered the market in 1998. On the free plan, you can shortlist profiles, send chat requests and reach out to up to 400 contacts, which is honestly more generous than a lot of competitors offer for free. Once that limit feels restrictive, the paid plans, Pro Lite and Pro, remove the cap entirely and throw in unlimited voice and video calling. The site also claims to have one of the lowest costs per contact around, which is worth checking if budget is a factor in your decision.5. LifePartner.inLifePartner.in maintains simplicity in the sense that the entire concept behind it is to help people meet someone truly serious and not just browse. So, both profile creation and search are detailed processes from the beginning. This website does not have a lot of extras; everything is kept as simple and direct as possible, starting from profile creation and ending with search and meeting the person who has a matching background.Which One Should You Pick?In truth, there is no single site that can be considered the best choice for all families; it all depends on the priorities of each family – is it the size of the database, the cost, or someone to guide them through the process? For those who value community and a personal approach, sites specialized for Punjabi Matrimony, such as Royal Matrimonial, will work better than one-size-fits-all platforms.

stories.primary_headline: Former finance minister questions J&K Bank’s faster lending growth outside UT

primary_source.headline: Former finance minister questions J&K Bank’s faster lending growth outside UT
primary_source.content: Srinagar: Former finance minister and Apni Party president Altaf Bukhari has questioned why Jammu and Kashmir Bank’s lending is growing more than three times faster outside the Union Territory than in its traditional home market, as the lender expands its national footprint.The bank’s March 2026 figures show advances in the UT rose 9.3 per cent, from Rs 69,694 crore in March 2025 to Rs 76,159 crore a year later.High Court quashes Jammu and Kashmir Bank officer’s dismissal over alleged anti-India campaignIn the rest of the country, including Ladakh, advances jumped 30.9 per cent, from Rs 37,292 crore to Rs 48,822 crore.Bukhari said the disparity raised questions about the bank’s strategy, particularly as the home market continues to account for the bulk of its business.He also claimed that NPAs outside the region were four to five times higher and questioned why lending was being expanded faster there.The bank’s published figures do not support that claim as an aggregate NPA-ratio comparison. Gross NPAs at the end of March stood at Rs 2,332 crore in the UT and Rs 793 crore outside it.Against the respective loan books, the gross NPA ratio works out to about 3.1 per cent and 1.6 per cent, respectively.The lending shift, however, is clear. The bank added Rs 6,465 crore to its home-market advances during 2025-26, compared with Rs 11,530 crore outside the region.The composition of the two portfolios is also markedly different. Corporate loans account for 73 per cent of advances outside the UT, against 7 per cent at home, where personal loans make up 49 per cent.Bukhari also questioned whether reported changes in recruitment could reduce opportunities for local youth.J&K: 11 IPS officers transferred, police chiefs for Kashmir and Jammu zones replacedHe said the bank had traditionally recruited people from the UT for posts outside it, except where local hiring was required.He further raised concerns over reports of a possible shift of the headquarters from Srinagar.The lender now operates across 18 states and four Union Territories. Yet the home market still accounts for 60.9 per cent of its advances and more than four-fifths of its deposits.
